facts.fact: The Krause Music Store is a commercial building on North Lincoln Avenue in Chicago.
facts.quote: The Krause Music Store is a commercial building at 4611 North Lincoln Avenue in Chicago, Illinois, United States.

facts.fact: Built in 1922, it was the last of the 126 buildings designed by Louis Sullivan.
facts.quote: Constructed in 1922, it is the last of the 126 buildings designed by Louis Sullivan.

facts.fact: Its façade, with curving plant-like forms framing the picture window, grew out of Sullivan's belief in organic architecture.
facts.quote: With its curvilinear plant-like forms and intricate framing of the picture window, the façade of this building is an outgrowth of Sullivan's belief in organic architecture.

facts.fact: William Krause's neighbour, architect William Presto, who had once drafted for Sullivan, designed the building and asked Sullivan to design its green terracotta façade.
facts.quote: Krause chose his neighbor, architect William Presto, to design the building (years earlier, Presto had worked as a draftsman for Louis Sullivan). Sullivan was asked by his former employee to design what would become the building's green terra cotta façade.

facts.fact: Sullivan ornamented the whole terracotta façade with geometric and curving forms taken from nature.
facts.quote: Showcasing his expertise with terra cotta, Sullivan designed the ornamentation of the entire façade with geometric and curvilinear forms of nature.

facts.fact: The store sold pianos and sheet music and was an early retailer of radios.
facts.quote: The store opened to sell pianos and sheet music and was a pioneering retailer for the introduction of the radio.

facts.fact: Chicago made the façade a city landmark in 1977.
facts.quote: On September 20, 1977, the City of Chicago recognized the historic significance of the building and designated the façade as a Chicago Landmark.

facts.fact: Owners who bought it in 2005 carefully restored the Sullivan façade.
facts.quote: In May 2005, the building was purchased by Pooja and Peter Vukosavich, who painstakingly restored the historic Sullivan façade and completed a modern renovation of the main floor for their company offices, Studio V Design – a marketing communications and design agency.

facts.fact: It was placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2006.
facts.quote: In 2006, through the efforts of Peter and Pooja Vukosavich, the building was placed in the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: The George H. Fallon Federal Office Building is an office building in Baltimore, Maryland.
facts.quote: George H. Fallon Federal Office Building, is a historic office building located at Baltimore, Maryland, United States.

facts.fact: Built from 1963 to 1967, it is a 17-storey International Style building with a steel and reinforced concrete frame, clad in granite panels from Minnesota.
facts.quote: It was built between 1963 and 1967, and is a 17-story, International Style steel frame and reinforced concrete building clad in granite panels from Minnesota.

facts.fact: It was built as part of Charles Center, a large urban renewal project carried out between 1955 and 1975.
facts.quote: It was developed as part of Charles Center, a major urban renewal project that was planned and implemented between 1955 and 1975.

facts.fact: The building is 480 feet long and 223 feet wide.
facts.quote: The building measures 480 feet long by 223 feet wide, and contains over 725,000 gross square feet of space.

facts.fact: It holds offices for several federal agencies.
facts.quote: It houses offices for a number of federal agencies, including the Federal Highway Administration and United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

facts.fact: It was named after Congressman George Hyde Fallon in 1971.
facts.quote: Public Law 91-653 officially designated the building as the "George H. Fallon Federal Office Building" in January 1971, in recognition of Congressman George Hyde Fallon (1902–1980).

facts.fact: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2023.
facts.quote: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 2023.

facts.fact: The building in Columbia, South Carolina, was designed by Marcel Breuer and completed in 1979, and served for 25 years as a federal courthouse.
facts.quote: Designed by Marcel Breuer and completed in 1979, it served for twenty-five years as a courthouse of the United States District Court for the District of South Carolina.

facts.fact: It is a Brutalist building of concrete, granite and glass.
facts.quote: The building is a Brutalist building made of concrete, granite, and glass.

facts.fact: Breuer designed it with his architectural partner Herbert Beckhard.
facts.quote: To complete the design of the new federal building and courthouse in Columbia, South Carolina, Breuer collaborated with his architectural partner Herbert Beckhard.

facts.fact: It combines a tall office tower with a long, low courthouse and a landscaped plaza.
facts.quote: Combining a tall office tower with a long, low courthouse and landscaped plaza, the complex's form is similar to that of many Modern-era federal buildings.

facts.fact: The tower's repeated windows carry peaked hoods (brise-soleils) that cut direct sun and keep the interior cooler in South Carolina's summers.
facts.quote: Unlike elaborate federal buildings from earlier eras, the tower is stark and unadorned, with its dominant design being repetitive windows with peaked hoods called brise soleils. The hoods serve to minimize direct sunlight, thus reducing the interior temperature during warm South Carolina summers.

facts.fact: It has a steel frame clad in precast concrete panels and dark grey granite.
facts.quote: The building has a steel frame and is clad in pre-cast concrete panels and dark gray cold spring natural granite.

facts.fact: A tunnel links the tower to the three-storey courthouse, and Breuer repeated the same window form on both.
facts.quote: A tunnel connects the office tower to the three-story courthouse building. Breuer unified the complex by repeating the same window form on the courthouse.

facts.fact: In the sunken courtyard Breuer designed a reflecting pool, softened with grass, shrubs and trees.
facts.quote: He designed a reflecting pool in the sunken courtyard, with grass panels, shrubs, and trees added to soften hardscape features.

facts.fact: It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: It is named for long-time Senator Strom Thurmond, and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: Haydarpaşa station in Istanbul was the city's main terminal for trains to and from Anatolia until 2012.
facts.quote: Haydarpaşa station (Turkish: Haydarpaşa Garı) is a railway station in Istanbul, that was, until 2012 the main city terminal for trains travelling to and from the Anatolian side of Turkey.

facts.fact: A larger building was needed after Haydarpaşa became the northern end of the Baghdad and Hejaz railways in 1904.
facts.quote: Haydarpaşa was chosen as the northern terminus for the Baghdad Railway and the Hejaz Railway in 1904, and, with rail traffic increasing, a larger building was required.

facts.fact: The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects, Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu, who chose a Neoclassical design; construction began in 1906.
facts.quote: The Anatolian Railway hired two German architects, Otto Ritter and Helmut Conu, to build the new building. They chose a Neo-classical design and construction started in 1906.

facts.fact: Its foundation rests on 1,100 wooden piles, each 21 metres long, driven into the soft shore.
facts.quote: Its foundation is based on 1100 wooden piles, each 21 metres (69 ft) long, driven into the soft shore by a steam hammer.

facts.fact: German and Italian stonemasons carved the exterior decoration.
facts.quote: German and Italian stonemasons crafted the decoration of the exterior.

facts.fact: Built on land reclaimed from the sea, the terminal opened on 4 November 1909.
facts.quote: The work was completed on land reclaimed from the sea on 19 August 1909 and the new terminal was inaugurated on 4 November 1909 for the birthday of Mehmed V.

facts.fact: A fire in 2010 destroyed the station's roof and fourth floor.
facts.quote: On 28 November 2010 a fire caused by carelessness during restoration work destroyed the station's roof and the 4th floor.

facts.fact: After the fire the original timber roof trusses were rebuilt and the stone façades cleaned of salt from the sea.
facts.quote: The station’s original roof structure, historically built with baroque-influenced timber trusses, was reconstructed. Stone façades were treated with low-pressure micro-abrasion cleaning, followed by desalination procedures to address extensive salt crystallization due to proximity to the sea.

facts.fact: Emperor Justinian I commissioned Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles to design the cathedral of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, built from 532 to 537.
facts.quote: Isidore of Miletus (Greek: Ἰσίδωρος ὁ Μιλήσιος; Medieval Greek pronunciation: [iˈsiðoros o miˈlisios]; Latin: Isidorus Miletus) was one of the two main Byzantine Greek mathematician, physicist and architects (Anthemius of Tralles was the other) that Emperor Justinian I commissioned to design the cathedral Hagia Sophia in Constantinople from 532 to 537.

facts.fact: Neither architect was formally trained in architecture; both were scientists able to organise thousands of workers and huge loads of rare materials from across the Roman Empire.
facts.quote: Although Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles were not formally educated in architecture, they were scientists who could organize the logistics of drawing thousands of labourers and unprecedented loads of rare raw materials from around the Roman Empire to construct the Hagia Sophia for Emperor Justinian I.

facts.fact: Stone came from as far as Egypt, Syria and Libya, and columns from several temples in Rome.
facts.quote: Isidore and Anthemius obtained stone from as far away as Egypt, Syria, and Libya, and columns from several temples in Rome.

facts.fact: To resist fire, Justinian had the church built of brick and mortar bound with iron, using no wood.
facts.quote: Emperor Justinian I ensured that his new structure would not be burned down, like its predecessors, by commissioning architects that would build the church mainly out of stone, rather than wood, “He compacted it of baked brick and mortar, and in many places bound it together with iron, but made no use of wood, so that the church should no longer prove combustible.”

facts.fact: Isidore is believed to have done much of the work on the domes, drawing on his study of vaults.
facts.quote: It is believed that Isidore did much of the work on the domes of the Hagia Sophia due to his extensive work on vaults, and his commentary, "On Vaulting".

facts.fact: The design combined the long plan of a Roman basilica with a central dome; after earthquakes in 553 and 557, parts of the dome collapsed in 558.
facts.quote: The Hagia Sophia architects innovatively combined the longitudinal structure of a Roman basilica and the central plan of a drum-supported dome, in order to withstand the high magnitude earthquakes of the Marmara region, “However, in May 558, little more than 20 years after the Church’s dedication, following the earthquakes of August 553 and December 557, parts of the central dome and its supporting structure system collapsed.” The Hagia Sophia was repeatedly cracked by earthquakes and was quickly repaired.

facts.fact: Isidore the Younger, Isidore's nephew, rebuilt the dome with ribs, the form seen today.
facts.quote: Isidore of Miletus’ nephew, Isidore the Younger, introduced the new dome design that can be viewed in the Hagia Sophia in present-day Istanbul, Turkey. Originally the dome was constructed without ribs, but achieved its present-day construction with ribs when Isidore the Younger repaired the church.

facts.fact: After an earthquake ruined the dome in 989, Trdat the Architect organised repairs, finished by 994.
facts.quote: After a great earthquake in 989 ruined the dome of Hagia Sophia, the Byzantine officials summoned Trdat the Architect to Byzantium to organize repairs. The restored dome was completed by 994. == References == == Sources == Cakmak, AS; Taylor, RM; Durukal, E (2009).

facts.fact: The Lütfi Kırdar centre, first called the Istanbul Sports and Exhibition Hall, is a convention complex in the Harbiye district of Istanbul.
facts.quote: Istanbul Lütfi Kırdar International Convention and Exhibition Center, often referred as Istanbul Lütfi Kırdar ICEC, shortly ICEC, (Turkish: İstanbul Lütfi Kırdar Uluslararası Kongre ve Sergi Sarayı), formerly Istanbul Sports and Exhibition Hall (İstanbul Spor ve Sergi Sarayı), is a multi-purpose convention complex located in Harbiye neighborhood of Şişli district in Istanbul, Turkey.

facts.fact: The city had no indoor venue fit to host the 1949 European Wrestling Championships.
facts.quote: However, the city lacked an indoor sports venue appropriate for this event.

facts.fact: Italian architect Paolo Vietti-Violi and Turkish architects Şinasi Şahingiray and Fazıl Aysu, who had also designed the Dolmabahçe Stadium, prepared the project.
facts.quote: Italian architect Paolo Vietti-Violi (1882-1965) and the Turkish architects Şinasi Şahingiray and Fazıl Aysu, who had designed also the Dolmabahçe Stadium in 1939, prepared the project.

facts.fact: Ground was broken on 30 January 1948.
facts.quote: The groundbreaking of the Istanbul Sports and Exhibition Hall building took place on January 30, 1948 in presence of the city's governor and mayor Lütfi Kırdar (1887-1961).

facts.fact: It opened on 3 June 1949 for the European Wrestling Championships.
facts.quote: Right after the completion of the construction, it was opened on June 3, 1949 to host the European Wrestling Championships.

facts.fact: Its grand hall seated 7,000 people and hosted sports from basketball to ice hockey, as well as circus shows.
facts.quote: In the center's grand hall with a seating capacity of 7,000 people, many different national and international sports events took place, such as basketball, handball, volleyball, boxing, weightlifting, wrestling, ice skating, ice hockey and dancing competitions as well as circus shows.

facts.fact: For many years it was the country's only indoor sports and exhibition hall.
facts.quote: Remaining the country's only indoor sports and exhibition hall for many years, it hosted fairs, concerts, meetings and exhibitions by utilizing the other halls when needed.

facts.fact: In 1996 it was turned into a convention centre for the UN Habitat II conference.
facts.quote: In 1996, the hall was transformed into a convention center to host the Habitat II, the Second United Nations Conference on Human Settlements, and was renamed then "Istanbul Lütfi Kırdar International Convention and Exhibition Center" (ICEC).

facts.fact: For the 2009 IMF and World Bank meeting, it was extended with a nine-level underground structure of 120,000 m².
facts.quote: For hosting the 2009 IMF and World Bank Group Annual Meeting, the center was expanded with a nine-level underground submerged structure of 120,000 m2 (1,300,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: At 435 metres, Milad Tower in Tehran is the tallest tower in Iran.
facts.quote: Milad Tower is 435 meters (1,427 ft) tall and is the tallest tower in Iran, and the sixth-tallest telecommunication tower in the world.

facts.fact: The design was led by Iranian architect Mohammad Reza Hafezi.
facts.quote: The design of the project was headed by Iranian architect Mohammad Reza Hafezi.

facts.fact: Construction was finished in 2007, eleven years after it began, and the tower opened on 7 October 2008.
facts.quote: The tower's construction was finished in 2007, 11 years after the beginning of construction. On 7 October 2008, Milad Tower was opened with the slogan "Heaven is near" in the presence of representatives of the Islamic Council, members of the Islamic Council of Tehran and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the mayor of Tehran.

facts.fact: It has five main parts: foundation, lobby structure, shaft, head and antenna mast.
facts.quote: It consists of five main parts, including the foundation, transition (lobby) structure, shaft, head structure and the antenna mast.

facts.fact: The concrete shaft rises about 315 metres from the ground floor.
facts.quote: The shaft is a concrete structure about 315 metres (1,033 ft) high from the ground floor.

facts.fact: The head is a steel structure of 12 floors weighing about 25,000 tonnes.
facts.quote: The head of the tower is a steel structure weighing about 25,000 tonnes and consisting of 12 floors.

facts.fact: Its top floors hold an art gallery, a revolving restaurant and open and closed observation decks, among other spaces.
facts.quote: The top floors of the tower include a public art gallery, a cafeteria, a revolving restaurant, a VIP restaurant, telecommunication floors, mechanical floors, fire-immune areas built as a refuge zone, a closed observation deck, an open observation deck, and a sky dome.

facts.fact: The octagonal base refers to traditional Iranian architecture.
facts.quote: The Milad Tower has an octagonal base, a reference to traditional Iranian architecture. === Selection of the location === To select the best location for the construction of the tower, 21 locations in Tehran were carefully examined from all angles, of which 4 locations (Abbas Abad, Lavizan, Yousef Abad, and Nasr area) were selected.

facts.fact: It is part of Tehran's International Trade and Convention Center, with a hotel, convention centre and IT park.
facts.quote: The tower is a part of the International Trade and Convention Center of Tehran, which also includes a five-star hotel, a convention center, a world trade center, and an IT park.

facts.fact: The Tomb of Ferdowsi in Tus, Iran, honours the Persian poet with a white marble base and a decorative edifice.
facts.quote: The Tomb of Ferdowsi (Persian: آرامگاه فردوسی, romanized: Ârâmgâh-e Ferdowsi) is a tomb complex composed of a white marble base, and a decorative edifice erected in honour of the Persian poet Ferdowsi located in Tus, Razavi Khorasan province, Iran.

facts.fact: Built in the early 1930s, it mainly draws on Achaemenid architecture to show Iran's culture and history.
facts.quote: It was built in the early 1930s, and mainly uses elements of Achaemenid architecture to demonstrate Iran's rich culture and history.

facts.fact: Haj Hossein Lurzadeh made the original design; the present design is credited mainly to Karim Taherzadeh, who replaced Lurzadeh's dome with a modern cubic form.
facts.quote: The tomb was originally designed by the Iranian architect, Haj Hossein Lurzadeh who aside from Ferdowsi's tomb also created some 842 mosques, as well as the private palace of Ramsar, part of the decoration of the Marmar palace, the Imam Hossein Mosque in Tehran, the Motahari Mosque, and various parts of the Hazrat-i-Seyyed-o-Shouhada shrine in Karbala, Iraq. The present design of the structure is credited mainly to Karim Taherzadeh, who replaced the old dome-shaped design by Lurzadeh with a modern cubical design.

facts.fact: The tomb resembles the tomb of Cyrus the Great and is built in the style of Achaemenid architecture.
facts.quote: Ferdowsi's tomb, which resembles the tomb of Cyrus the Great, is built in style of Achaemenid architecture.

facts.fact: It stands at the centre of a Persian four-part (Char-bagh) garden.
facts.quote: The basic structure of the tomb is rectangular with a large garden surrounding the structure and interacting with the structure in the Persian style of gardening known as Char-bagh (or Chaharbagh translating to four gardens in Persian).

facts.fact: The edifice is a wide chamber at the base with a cube on top, surrounded by four pillars and decorated with scenes and text from the Shahnameh.
facts.quote: The edifice can be divided into a "wide chamber" that lies at the base and a cubical erection on top, with four pillars surrounding it and scenes from the epic of Shahnameh and text ornating it.

facts.fact: The poet is buried in the centre of the wide chamber beneath the cube.
facts.quote: The body of the poet is actually interred in the center of the rectangular wide chamber underneath the overlying four pillars cube.

facts.fact: Its frieze columns carry a two-horned bull motif that closely imitates the columns of Persepolis.
facts.quote: Each frieze column has a box, followed by a two horn bull sign which is very much similar if not the exact imitation of the Persepolis column design.

facts.fact: Inside, Feraydoon Sadeghi carved deep relief scenes from the Shahnameh around the poet's tombstone.
facts.quote: The chief architect responsible for the design of the interior of the tomb of Ferdowsi is Feraydoon Sadeghi who created deep frieze scenes using three dimensional statues each depicting a scene from Shahnameh.

facts.fact: The Tomb of Saadi in Shiraz, Iran, is a mausoleum complex dedicated to the Persian poet Saadi.
facts.quote: The Tomb of Saadi (Persian: آرامگاه سعدی شیرازی) is a tomb and mausoleum complex dedicated to the Persian poet Saadi, commonly known as Saadieh (Persian: سعدیه). The complex is located in the city of Shiraz, in the province of Fars, Iran.

facts.fact: The current building was built between 1950 and 1952 to a design by Mohsen Foroughi, inspired by the Chehel Sotoun and mixing old and new architectural elements.
facts.quote: The current building was constructed between 1950 and 1952 to a design by the architect Mohsen Foroughi and was inspired by the Chehel Sotoun with a fusion of old and new architectural elements.

facts.fact: It has eight brown stone pillars at the front, and the main structure is made of white stone and tiles.
facts.quote: It includes eight brown stone pillars at the front of the tomb. The main structure is made of white stones and tiles.

facts.fact: Cubic from outside, it is an octagon inside, with marble walls and an azure arch.
facts.quote: The building of the tomb of Saadi Shirazi has a cubic shape from the outside, and from the inside, it is in the form of an octagon with walls of marble and an azure arch.

facts.fact: The tomb sits where two perpendicular terraces meet, inside an octagonal building topped by a blue dome.
facts.quote: The main building of the tomb includes two terraces that are perpendicular to each other. The tomb of Saadi is located at the angle of these terraces, inside an octagonal building on top of which stands an amazing azure blue dome.

facts.fact: The façade is travertine and the interior marble.
facts.quote: The facade of the tomb is made of travertine stone, and the interior is made of marble. === Water features === A fish pond lies on the left side of the tomb of Saadi Shirazi.

facts.fact: It was added to Iran's National Heritage List in 1975.
facts.quote: The complex was added to the Iran National Heritage List on 9 December 1975, administered by the Cultural Heritage, Handicrafts and Tourism Organization of Iran. == History == Saadi was buried at the end of his life at a khanqah at the current location.

facts.fact: The Sursock Museum is a modern and contemporary art museum in Beirut.
facts.quote: The Sursock Museum (Arabic: قصر سرسق), officially known as the Nicolas Ibrahim Sursock Museum, is a modern and contemporary art museum in Beirut, Lebanon.

facts.fact: The museum occupies a private villa built in 1912 by Nicolas Ibrahim Sursock, who asked in his will that it become a museum.
facts.quote: In 1912, the Lebanese aristocrat Nicolas Ibrahim Sursock built the private villa that now houses the museum. He decreed in his will that the villa be transformed into a museum.

facts.fact: The building mixes Italianate (Venetian) and Ottoman influences, and is one of the few villas of its time left in Beirut.
facts.quote: The Sursock Museum building exemplifies Lebanese architecture, with its Italianate (specifically Venetian) and Ottoman architectural influences. It is one of the few remaining villas from its epoch in Beirut.

facts.fact: The museum opened in 1961.
facts.quote: The museum opened in 1961, directed by Amine Beyhum, with an exhibit of works of contemporary Lebanese artists, setting a precedent for cultural events in Beirut.

facts.fact: It was expanded with four new underground floors beneath the garden, designed by Jean-Michel Wilmotte and Jacques Abou Khaled.
facts.quote: The museum was expanded with four new underground floors beneath the current garden, at a cost of US$12 million. French architect Jean-Michel Wilmotte and Lebanese architect Jacques Abou Khaled designed the expansion project.

facts.fact: The extension grew the museum from 1,500 to 8,500 square metres, adding galleries, a research library, an auditorium and a restoration workshop.
facts.quote: The project increased the museum's area from 1,500 square meters to 8,500 square meters and opened additional exhibition spaces, a research library, an auditorium, a restoration workshop, new storage spaces for the collection, as well as a store and restaurant.

facts.fact: The museum reopened on 8 October 2015.
facts.quote: The museum reopened on 8 October 2015.

facts.fact: The ammonium nitrate explosion of 4 August 2020 badly damaged the museum, and 57 artworks had to be restored.
facts.quote: On 4 August 2020, the museum sustained significant damage as a result of a catastrophic ammonium nitrate explosion. 57 artworks were damaged and had to be restored.

facts.fact: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque, also called the Blue Mosque, is a Sunni mosque in downtown Beirut, 72 m high.
facts.quote: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque (Arabic: جامع محمد الأمين), also referred to as the Blue Mosque, is a Sunni mosque, 72 m high, minarets´ roof of 65 m high and main dome spire of 48 m high and its roof 42 m, is located in downtown Beirut, Lebanon.

facts.fact: It stands next to the Maronite Cathedral of Saint George and was inaugurated in 2008.
facts.quote: The mosque was inaugurated in 2008, and is located adjacent to the Maronite Cathedral of Saint George. == History == In the 19th century, a zawiya, named after Sheikh Abu Nasr al-Yafi, was built on this site.

facts.fact: Its foundation was laid in November 2002 after a donation by Prime Minister Rafic Hariri.
facts.quote: Soon after the Lebanon Civil War, following a donation by the late Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, the foundation for the Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque was laid in November 2002.

facts.fact: Digging for the mosque uncovered part of the main Roman east–west street, with paving and columns.
facts.quote: During the construction of the mosque, archaeologists uncovered a section of the east–west main Roman street (Decumanus Maximus), with paving and columns.

facts.fact: Azmi Fakhoury designed it in a style close to Ottoman architecture; it holds up to 6,400 worshippers.
facts.quote: Designed by Azmi Fakhoury in a style similar to the architecture of Ottoman Turk, the mosque can accommodate up to 6,400 worshippers.

facts.fact: It has five domes, all made of light blue tiles.
facts.quote: The Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque contains five domes, all of which are made from light blue tiles.

facts.fact: The 2020 Beirut explosion badly damaged the mosque, shattering its chandeliers and windows.
facts.quote: On August 4, 2020, the mosque was badly damaged by the Beirut explosions. Its chandeliers and windows were shattered, leaving broken glass on the floor. == Construction and design == Soon after the Lebanon Civil War, following a donation by the late Prime Minister Rafic Hariri, the foundation for the Mohammad Al-Amin Mosque was laid in November 2002.

facts.fact: The National Institutions House on King George Street in Jerusalem is the administrative headquarters of the Zionist movement's national institutions.
facts.quote: The National Institutions House (Hebrew: בית המוסדות הלאומיים) is a landmark complex on King George Street in downtown Jerusalem that serves as the administrative headquarters for the national institutions of the Zionist movement.

facts.fact: A 1927 architectural competition drew 37 proposals.
facts.quote: In 1927, an architectural competition was held and 37 proposals submitted.

facts.fact: The brief asked for a building of no more than two storeys, one structure in three sections, suited to the city's character.
facts.quote: The leadership of the National Institutions required that the building be no more than two stories in height, that it be a single structure divided into three sections (for the Zionist Executive—composed of the World Zionist Organization and the Jewish Agency for Israel—as well as the Jewish National Fund and Keren Hayesod), and the building be well-suited to the city's character.

facts.fact: Yohanan Ratner's winning design wraps the building around a large forecourt, giving it a formal presence and shielding it from street noise.
facts.quote: The design selected was that of the architect Yohanan Ratner, who wrapped the structure around a large forecourt in order to create a formal presence while isolating it from the noise from the street, as well as to maintain the impressive facade of the building despite its lowness in comparison to surrounding structures.

facts.fact: Ratner used the International Style but added elements unique to Jerusalem.
facts.quote: Ratner designed the building in the International Style, but included elements unique to Jerusalem.

facts.fact: Some outer elements echo the Tower of David, and the windows recall the slits in the Old City walls.
facts.quote: The building contains outer elements similar to those of the Tower of David and the windows are reminiscent of the slits in the Old City Walls

facts.fact: Building began in 1928 and went ahead in stages: the first floor was dedicated in 1930 and the second storey finished in 1936.
facts.quote: Construction work began in 1928. Due to budgetary problems, the construction was completed in stages. The first floor of the building was dedicated in 1930, and the second story was completed in 1936.

facts.fact: It was bombed in 1948 and hosted the first sessions of the Knesset.
facts.quote: The building holds profound historical significance: it was devastated in the 1948 Jewish Agency bombing, hosted the inaugural sessions of the Knesset, and served as the venue for the inauguration of Israel's first president, Chaim Weizmann.

facts.fact: The Jerusalem Great Synagogue is an Orthodox synagogue at 56 King George Street, Jerusalem.
facts.quote: The Jerusalem Great Synagogue (Hebrew: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת הַגָּדוֹל בּיְרוּשָׁלַיִם, romanized: Beit HaKnesset HaGadol b'Yerushalayim) is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 56 King George Street, Jerusalem, Israel.

facts.fact: A new, much larger synagogue was built when the hall at neighbouring Heichal Shlomo could no longer hold the worshippers.
facts.quote: Soon afterwards, when the premises could not hold the number of worshippers attending, it was decided that a new, much larger synagogue be built.

facts.fact: Its main sponsor was the British philanthropist Sir Isaac Wolfson.
facts.quote: The main sponsor for construction of the new synagogue was Sir Isaac Wolfson, a Jewish philanthropist from Britain.

facts.fact: It is dedicated to the six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust and to fallen Israeli soldiers.
facts.quote: The Wolfson family consecrated the synagogue in the memory of the six million Jews who were murdered in the Holocaust and to the fallen soldiers of Israel Defense Forces.

facts.fact: German-born architect Alexander Friedman modelled the building's style on the Jewish Temple.
facts.quote: The style of the building was modeled on the Jewish Temple by German-born architect Alexander Friedman.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on Tu B'Av 1982.
facts.quote: The inauguration took place on Tu B'Av 1982.

facts.fact: The sanctuary seats 850 men and 550 women.
facts.quote: The sanctuary seats 850 men and 550 women.

facts.fact: KAUST is a public research university in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia.
facts.quote: The King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST; Arabic: جامعة الملك عبد الله للعلوم و التقنية jāmiʿat al-malik ʿabd al-Lāh li-l-ʿulūm wa-t-teqniyya) is a public research university located in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: The architecture firm HOK made the campus master plan, which included wind towers and solar panels.
facts.quote: They employed the Washington Advisory Group's Frank H. T. Rhodes and Frank Press to design the academic structure, SRI International to develop the four research institutes, and the architectural firm of HOK for the campus master plan, which included wind towers and solar panels.

facts.fact: The site covers 16.4 km² of land and 19.6 km² of marine sanctuary offshore.
facts.quote: The location of the campus at Thuwal included 16.4 sq km on land and 19.6 sq km of marine sanctuary offshore.

facts.fact: Ground was broken in October 2007.
facts.quote: Ground breaking took place in October 2007, and 178 scholarships were awarded in January 2008.

facts.fact: The core campus sits on the Red Sea and covers more than 36 km², including a marine sanctuary and research facilities.
facts.quote: The university's core campus, located on the Red Sea at Thuwal, is sited on more than 36 square kilometres (14 mi2), encompassing a marine sanctuary and research facilities.

facts.fact: It was Saudi Arabia's first LEED-certified project and is the world's largest LEED Platinum campus.
facts.quote: KAUST was Saudi Arabia's first LEED certified project and is the world's largest LEED Platinum campus.

facts.fact: The AIA Committee on the Environment named it one of the 2010 Top Ten Green Projects.
facts.quote: Designed by international architecture firm Hellmuth, Obata and Kassabaum, it was also chosen by the American Institute of Architects (AIA) Committee on the Environment (COTE) as one of the 2010 Top Ten Green Projects.

facts.fact: The university library won the 2011 AIA/ALA Library Building Award.
facts.quote: The university library received the 2011 AIA/ALA Library Building Award for accomplishments in library architecture.

facts.fact: At opening it became the first mixed-gender university campus in Saudi Arabia.
facts.quote: At its opening, KAUST became the first mixed-gender university campus in Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: The Riyadh TV Tower is a 170-metre television tower in the Al-Wisham neighbourhood of Riyadh.
facts.quote: The Riyadh TV Tower (Arabic: برج تلفزيون الرياض) is a 170-metre-high (560 ft) television tower in the Al-Wisham neighborhood of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1975 and was completed in 1982.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1975 and was completed in 1982.

facts.fact: It was Saudi Arabia's tallest structure from 1982 until 2000, when Al-Faisaliah Tower passed it.
facts.quote: It was the tallest structure in Saudi Arabia from 1982 until 2000, when it was surpassed by Al-Faisaliah Tower.

facts.fact: The Alexander Spendiaryan National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre, known locally as 'Opera', is an opera house in Yerevan.
facts.quote: The Alexander Spendiaryan National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre (Armenian: Ալեքսանդր Սպենդիարյանի անվան օպերայի և բալետի ազգային ակադեմիական թատրոն, romanized: Aleksandr Spendiaryani anvan operayi yev baleti azgayin akademiakan t’atron), simply known by locals as 'Opera', is an opera theatre in Yerevan.

facts.fact: The building was designed by architect Alexander Tamanian.
facts.quote: The opera building was designed by architect Alexander Tamanian.

facts.fact: It holds two halls: the Aram Khachaturian Concert Hall with 1,300 seats and the opera and ballet theatre with about 1,070.
facts.quote: It consists of two concert halls; after several renovations, the Aram Khachaturian Concert Hall offers 1300 seats and the Alexander Spendiaryan Opera and Ballet National Theatre about 1070 seats.

facts.fact: Ground was broken on 28 November 1930, for the 10th anniversary of Soviet Armenia.
facts.quote: The ground-breaking of the Opera Theatre took place on 28 November 1930 on the occasion of the 10th anniversary of Soviet Armenia.

facts.fact: It officially opened on 20 January 1933 with Spendiaryan's opera Almast.
facts.quote: It officially opened on 20 January 1933, with a performance of Alexander Spendiaryan's opera Almast; the venue is named after this composer.

facts.fact: The theatre hall was completed in 1939 to Tamanian's design, under his son's supervision.
facts.quote: Based on Tamanian's design and under the supervision of his son the theatre hall was completed in 1939.

facts.fact: Large-scale construction did not finish until 1953, when the whole building was completed.
facts.quote: Large-scale construction works did not finish until 1953, when the entire building was finally completed.

facts.fact: It became the National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre in 1956.
facts.quote: In 1956, the theatre received the status of National Academic Opera and Ballet Theatre.

facts.fact: Government House in Baku houses several Azerbaijani state ministries.
facts.quote: The Government House of Baku, also known as the House of Government, is a government building housing various state ministries of Azerbaijan.

facts.fact: It stands on Neftchiler Avenue facing Baku Boulevard, with its rear on Uzeyir Hajibeyov Street.
facts.quote: It is located on Neftchiler Avenue and faces the Baku Boulevard, while the rear of the building faces the busy Uzeyir Hajibeyov Street in central Baku.

facts.fact: It was designed for 5,500 people.
facts.quote: Government House was designed for 5,500 people.

facts.fact: In 1934 the Soviet authorities held a competition for the Baku Soviet Palace, later renamed Government House.
facts.quote: In 1934, the Soviet authorities announced a tender for the construction of the Baku Soviet Palace (later renamed the Government House).

facts.fact: Lev Rudnev and Vladimir Munts won the competition, with K. Tkachenko taking part.
facts.quote: The competition was won by well-known architects Lev Rudnev, Vladimir Munts and K. Tkachenko (participant).

facts.fact: With some changes to the project, it was built between 1936 and 1952.
facts.quote: With some alterations to the project, the building of the Government House was built between 1936 and 1952.

facts.fact: Building it also created Lenin Square, now Azadliq (Freedom) Square, in front of it.
facts.quote: The construction of the building also led to the construction of Lenin Square (later renamed Azadliq Square) in front of the Government House.

facts.fact: The government renovated it from 2006 to 2010.
facts.quote: In 2006, the government of Azerbaijan started renovation work on the building and completed the project in 2010.

facts.fact: The Parliament of Georgia Building, at 8 Rustaveli Avenue in Tbilisi, is the meeting place of Georgia's parliament.
facts.quote: The Parliament of Georgia Building (Georgian: საქართველოს პარლამენტის შენობა, romanized: sakartvelos p'arlament'is shenoba) is the meeting place of the Parliament of Georgia, located in Tbilisi, the capital of Georgia. It is located in 8 Rustaveli Avenue, close to the foothills of Mount Mtatsminda.

facts.fact: It was built as the House of Government of the Georgian SSR, on the site of the demolished 19th-century Alexander Nevsky Cathedral.
facts.quote: The building complex was constructed as the House of Government of Georgian SSR on the site of the demolished 19th-century Alexander Nevsky Cathedral and adjacent churchyard, with burials of the Georgian cadets killed during the Bolshevik invasion of 1921.

facts.fact: The complex has two buildings: the upper one, by Viktor Kokorin and Giorgi Lezhava, was built from 1933 to 1938, and the lower one on Rustaveli Avenue from 1946 to 1953.
facts.quote: It consists of two buildings; the "upper" building was designed by Viktor Kokorin and Giorgi Lezhava and built from 1933 to 1938. The "lower" building, along Rustaveli Avenue, was constructed by the same architects with an input from Vladimer Nasaridze from 1946 to 1953.

facts.fact: A courtyard with staircases and fountains connects the two buildings.
facts.quote: The two buildings are connected with a courtyard, with staircases and fountains.

facts.fact: Both buildings draw heavily on traditional Georgian architecture.
facts.quote: The design of both buildings heavily uses elements of traditional Georgian architecture.

facts.fact: The avenue front is dominated by a monumental arcade with massive eaves and an arch pediment.
facts.quote: The exterior facing the avenue is dominated by a monumental arcade, with massive eaves and "arch" pediment.

facts.fact: The buildings are lightweight reinforced concrete clad in tufa, granite and other stone.
facts.quote: The buildings are built of lightweight reinforced concrete, with exterior cladding of tufa rock, granite, and other materials.

facts.fact: Badly damaged in the 1991–92 coup, the complex was restored and served as the parliament's seat from 1997 to 2012.
facts.quote: The complex was severely damaged during the December 1991–January 1992 military coup, during which the beleaguered President Zviad Gamsakhurdia was entrenched in the underground bunker under the government premises. The building was subsequently restored, refurbished, and used as the seat of the Parliament of Georgia from 1997 to 2012, when the legislature moved to the newly constructed edifice in Kutaisi, Georgia's second most important city.

facts.fact: The Ismailiyya Palace on Istiglaliyyat Street in Baku now houses the Presidium of the Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan.
facts.quote: The Ismailiyya Palace (Azerbaijani: İsmailiyyə Sarayı) is a historical building that currently serves as the Presidium of the Academy of Sciences of Azerbaijan. It is on Istiglaliyyat Street in Baku.

facts.fact: Polish architect Józef Płoszko built it for a charity society, paid for by the millionaire Musa Naghiyev in memory of his son Ismayil, after whom it is named.
facts.quote: The palace was constructed for a Charity Society by Polish architect Józef Płoszko, at the expense of the millionaire Musa Naghiyev in commemoration of his deceased son Ismayil, and was named Ismailiyya after him.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1908 and ended in 1913.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1908 and ended in 1913.

facts.fact: It was Płoszko's first independent project in his 30 years in Baku, and remains his most iconic.
facts.quote: This was Płoszko’s first independent project during the 30 years he lived in Baku and remains his most iconic.

facts.fact: The building is in the Venetian Gothic style.
facts.quote: The building was constructed in the Venetian Gothic style.

facts.fact: Meetings and congresses were held in its white stone assembly hall, whose windows open onto the street.
facts.quote: After the opening ceremony, conferences of Muslim Charity Society members, meetings of Muslim women and Baku intelligentsia, and congresses of clergy were held in the building's white stone assembly hall. The hall's windows open onto Nikolayevskaya street.

facts.fact: Fire and fighting damaged it during the March Days of 1918; it was rebuilt in 1923 under the architect Dubov, who removed the sentences carved on the façades.
facts.quote: During the March Days in 1918 the building suffered damage from fire and warfare. In 1923, under the guidance of the architect Dubov, the building was reconstructed and the sentences on the front and side facades were removed.

facts.fact: The 28-storey Martinelli Building in São Paulo was the first skyscraper built in Brazil.
facts.quote: The Martinelli Building (in Portuguese: Edifício Martinelli), with 28 floors, is the first skyscraper built in Brazil.

facts.fact: It is 105 metres tall.
facts.quote: Located in São Paulo, it is 105 meters tall.

facts.fact: Italian-born entrepreneur Giuseppe Martinelli planned it in 1922.
facts.quote: The building was planned in 1922 by the Italian-born entrepreneur, Giuseppe Martinelli.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1924 and was completed in 1929.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1924, and was completed in 1929.

facts.fact: When it opened it was the tallest building in Latin America and the largest concrete-framed building in the world.
facts.quote: At the time of its opening, it was the tallest building in Latin America, and the largest concrete-framed building in the world.

facts.fact: Mayor Olavo Setúbal had it completely remodelled from 1975 to 1979.
facts.quote: The building was completely remodeled by Mayor Olavo Setúbal from 1975 to 1979.

facts.fact: Today it houses city housing and planning departments, with shops on the ground floor.
facts.quote: Today, the building houses the Departments of Municipal Housing and planning, companies Emurb and Cohab-SP, the headquarters of the Association of Banks of SP, and several shops on the ground floor of the building.

facts.fact: Mineirão, a football stadium in Belo Horizonte, is owned by the state of Minas Gerais and used by Cruzeiro.
facts.quote: Owned by the state of Minas Gerais, it is used by Cruzeiro Esporte Clube.

facts.fact: The stadium seats 66,658 spectators.
facts.quote: The stadium has a seating capacity of 66,658 spectators.

facts.fact: It was designed by architects Eduardo Mendes Guimarães Júnior and Caspar Garreto, with structural design by engineer Arthur Eugênio Jermann.
facts.quote: Mineirão was designed by the architects Eduardo Mendes Guimarães Júnior and Caspar Garreto. The structural design was prepared by the engineer Arthur Eugênio Jermann, and the construction work was directed by Gil César Moreira de Abreu.

facts.fact: About 5,000 people worked on it from 1963 until it opened on 5 September 1965.
facts.quote: From 1963 until the inauguration on 5 September 1965, about 5,000 people worked on the project.

facts.fact: Its engineering team studied Maracanã in detail to avoid repeating its structural weaknesses.
facts.quote: The Mineirão engineering team studied Maracanã in detail, looking for structural weaknesses that should not be repeated in Belo Horizonte.

facts.fact: The main challenge was the superstructure, a pseudo-ellipse 275 m long and 217 m wide, built with conventional equipment.
facts.quote: One of the main challenges was the construction of the superstructure, a pseudo-ellipse with a major axis of 275 m (902 ft) and a minor axis of 217 m (712 ft), using conventional equipment.

facts.fact: To test the design, the builders made a 'mini-Mineirão', a trial section of stands and roof put through different tests.
facts.quote: To test the design and reduce uncertainty, the builders created a "mini-Mineirão", known as experimental sector 15, where a section of the stands and roof was subjected to different kinds of tests.

facts.fact: Steel bars longer than local industry could supply were welded together on site.
facts.quote: The work required steel bars in lengths that local industry could not supply. The solution came on the construction site itself, where engineers and workers welded bars together to produce the required lengths.

facts.fact: It was a venue for the 2013 Confederations Cup and the 2014 FIFA World Cup.
facts.quote: It served as a venue in the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup and the 2014 FIFA World Cup.

facts.fact: The Maracanã, officially Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho, is a football stadium in Rio de Janeiro owned by the state government.
facts.quote: Estádio do Maracanã, officially known as Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho, is an association football stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Located in the Maracanã neighborhood, it is owned by the Rio de Janeiro state government and managed by the clubs Flamengo and Fluminense.

facts.fact: Rio's city government opened the design and construction competition in 1947; the contract went to a group including Michael Feldman, Waldir Ramos, Raphael Galvão, Oscar Valdetaro, Orlando Azevedo, Pedro Paulo Bernardes Bastos and Antônio Dias Carneiro.
facts.quote: The competition for the design and construction was opened by the municipality of Rio de Janeiro in 1947, with the construction contract awarded to engineer Humberto Menescal Michael Feldman, Waldir Ramos, Raphael Galvão, Oscar Valdetaro, Orlando Azevedo, Pedro Paulo Bernardes Bastos, and Antônio Dias Carneiro.

facts.fact: The cornerstone was laid on 2 August 1948, leaving under two years before the first World Cup game.
facts.quote: The first cornerstone was laid at the site of the stadium on 2 August 1948. With the first World Cup game scheduled to be played on 24 June 1950, this left a little under two years to finish construction.

facts.fact: It opened for the 1950 World Cup, where 173,850 spectators watched the deciding game, still the record attendance.
facts.quote: The stadium was opened in 1950 to host the FIFA World Cup, in which Brazil was beaten 2–1 by Uruguay in the deciding game, in front of a still standing record attendance of 173,850 spectators, on 16 July 1950.

facts.fact: Though in use from 1950, it was only fully completed in 1965.
facts.quote: Despite the stadium having come into use in 1950, the construction was only fully completed in 1965.

facts.fact: At the 1950 World Cup it overtook Hampden Park as the largest stadium in the world.
facts.quote: What is beyond dispute is that Maracanã overtook Hampden Park as the largest stadium in the world.

facts.fact: For the 2014 World Cup and 2016 Olympics, its original two-tier bowl was demolished and replaced by a mainly one-tier bowl.
facts.quote: For the 2014 World Cup and 2016 Olympics and Paralympics, a major reconstruction project was initiated in 2010. The original seating bowl, with a two-tier configuration, was demolished, giving way to a new primarily one-tier seating bowl with a space for 78,639 spectators.

facts.fact: The original concrete roof was replaced by a PTFE-coated fibreglass membrane covering 95% of the seats.
facts.quote: The original stadium's roof in concrete was removed and replaced with a fiberglass tensioned membrane coated with polytetra-fluoroethylene. The new roof covers 95% of the seats inside the stadium, unlike the former design, where protection was only afforded to some seats in the upper ring and the bleachers above the gate access of each sector.

facts.fact: The Teatro Amazonas is an opera house in Manaus, Brazil.
facts.quote: The Amazon Theatre (Portuguese: Teatro Amazonas) is an opera house located in Manaus, Brazil.

facts.fact: The chosen design came from the Gabinete Português de Engenharia e Arquitectura, an engineering and architecture office in Lisbon.
facts.quote: The chosen project was made by the Gabinete Português de Engenharia e Arquitectura, an engineering and architecture office from Lisbon.

facts.fact: Construction was ready to begin in 1884 under the Italian architect Celestial Sacardim.
facts.quote: By 1884, construction was ready to begin under the Italian architect Celestial Sacardim.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 31 December 1896.
facts.quote: The theatre was inaugurated on December 31, 1896, with the first performance occurring on January 7, 1897, with the Italian opera, La Gioconda, by Amilcare Ponchielli.

facts.fact: Its style is considered Renaissance Revival.
facts.quote: The theatre's architectural style is considered typically Renaissance Revival.

facts.fact: Roof tiles came from Alsace, steel walls from Glasgow and Carrara marble from Italy.
facts.quote: The roofing tiles were imported from Alsace, the steel walls from Glasgow, Scotland and the Carrara marble for the stairs, statues and columns, from Italy.

facts.fact: The dome is covered with 36,000 decorated ceramic tiles painted in the colours of Brazil's flag.
facts.quote: The dome is covered with 36,000 decorated ceramic tiles painted in the colors of the national flag of Brazil.

facts.fact: The auditorium seats 701 people.
facts.quote: The Auditorium seats 701 persons.

facts.fact: In July 2026 UNESCO named it a World Heritage Site together with the Teatro da Paz.
facts.quote: In July 2026, it was designated by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site along with Teatro da Paz.

facts.fact: The Vila Velha Theater is a performing arts centre in Salvador, Bahia.
facts.quote: The Vila Velha Theater (Portuguese: Teatro Vila Velha), also known simply as "Vila", is a performing arts center in Salvador, Bahia, Brazil.

facts.fact: Built in 1964, it stands on Avenida Sete, west of the 19th-century Passeio Público.
facts.quote: The theater was constructed in 1964 and is located on Avenida Sete, at the west of the 19th-century Neoclassical public area, the Passeio Público.

facts.fact: The Bahia state government granted the site in the public promenade in 1961.
facts.quote: The state government of Bahia granted a space in the Public Promenade in 1961 for the construction of the new theater.

facts.fact: Architect Silvio Robatto designed it in the Modern style.
facts.quote: The theater was designed by the architect Silvio Robatto (1935-2008) and built in the Modern style.

facts.fact: Its style contrasts sharply with the Neoclassical buildings of the Passeio Público and the Palácio da Aclamação.
facts.quote: The style is in stark contrast to the numerous 19th century Neoclassical structures of the Passeio Publico, and of the Palácio da Aclamação.

facts.fact: The main hall can be rearranged for each kind of show and holds up to 350 people.
facts.quote: Its configuration can be changed according to the genre of presentation, but holds up to 350 people.

facts.fact: It was a centre of the Tropicália movement and of cultural opposition to Brazil's military dictatorship.
facts.quote: The theater was a center of the 1960s counterculture movement, Tropicália, and cultural opposition to the Military dictatorship in Brazil (1964-1985).

facts.fact: A large-scale renovation of the building took place in 1998.
facts.quote: A large-scale renovation of the theater building followed in 1998.

facts.fact: The Municipal Market of São Paulo is a large public market in the city's historic centre.
facts.quote: The Municipal Market of São Paulo (Portuguese: Mercado Municipal Paulistano, or Mercado Municipal de São Paulo) is a large public market in São Paulo, Brazil.

facts.fact: Architect Francisco Ramos de Azevedo designed it, and it opened on 25 January 1933 as a wholesale and retail market for food.
facts.quote: It was designed by the architect Francisco Ramos de Azevedo and inaugurated on January 25, 1933 as a wholesale and retail post specializing in fruits, vegetables, cereals, meats, spices, and other food products.

facts.fact: It stands near the Tamanduateí River on the old Várzea do Carmo floodplain.
facts.quote: It is located near the Tamanduateí River in the old Várzea do Carmo, a floodplain of the river now primarily used as Dom Pedro II Park.

facts.fact: The market covers 12,600 square metres, with shops on the ground floor and restaurants on the mezzanine.
facts.quote: The first floor of the market is occupied by retailers, and the second floor mezzanine serves as a restaurant. The Mercadão occupies 12,600 square metres (136,000 ft2) and has 1,500 employees working at various in the building.

facts.fact: Its façade is the work of Felisberto Ranzini, who worked in Ramos de Azevedo's office, and mixes Ionic and Doric columns.
facts.quote: The façade of the Municipal Market is the work of Felisberto Ranzini (1882–1976), an Italian-Brazilian who worked in the architectural office of Ramos de Azevedo. Ranzini, who also participated in the construction of the São Francisco Law School, utilized a mix of Ionic and Doric columns on the municipal market.

facts.fact: The massive columns leave room for large areas of glazing that bring in plenty of daylight.
facts.quote: The massive columns allow for large spaces for glazing in the market which in turn provide a large source of natural light.

facts.fact: Its 72 stained-glass pieces, in 32 panels, are by Conrado Sorgenicht Filho and his studio.
facts.quote: 72 stained glass, arranged in 32 panels, are the work of the artist Conrado Sorgenicht Filho and his office, Casa Conrado Sorgenicht.

facts.fact: Unlike church glass, the windows show food production around São Paulo.
facts.quote: Unlike stained glass produced as sacred works, the windows of the market depict various aspects of food production in the greater São Paulo region.

facts.fact: A renovation finished in 2004 added a 2,000 m² mezzanine with eight restaurants and a granite floor.
facts.quote: A new 2,000 square metres (22,000 ft2) mezzanine with eight restaurants, new exterior lighting, and the replacement of the market floor with granite slabs were completed by August 2004. == References == == External links == Media related to Municipal Market of São Paulo at Wikimedia Commons

facts.fact: The Matarazzo Building, also called Palácio do Anhangabaú, is São Paulo's city hall.
facts.quote: Matarazzo Building (Portuguese: Edifício Matarazzo), also known as Palácio do Anhangabaú (Anhangabaú Palace), is the city hall of the city of São Paulo, Brazil.

facts.fact: It belonged to the bank Banespa until 2004, when it was sold to the city government.
facts.quote: It belonged to Banespa until 2004, when it was sold to the city government.

facts.fact: Italian architect Marcello Piacentini designed it for Ermelino Matarazzo, as the headquarters of his industries.
facts.quote: It was designed by Italian architect Marcello Piacentini under the will of Ermelino Matarazzo, in order to host the headquarters of his industries.

facts.fact: Its architectural style looks like Art Deco.
facts.quote: The building's architectural style looks like Art Deco.

facts.fact: Francisco Ramos de Azevedo designed São Paulo's Justice Palace, among many other city buildings.
facts.quote: He also designed the Municipal Theater, the Municipal Market of São Paulo, the Industries Palace, the Justice Palace, the Postal Office building, the Sion School, among other buildings.

facts.fact: The Ulysses Guimarães Convention Center, formerly the Brasília Convention Center, is a convention centre in Brasília.
facts.quote: The Ulysses Guimarães Convention Center (Portuguese: Centro de Convenções Ulysses Guimarães, CCUG), formerly the Brasília Convention Center (Portuguese: Centro de Convenções de Brasília) is a convention center located in Brasília.

facts.fact: Sérgio Bernardes designed it in 1973; it opened on 12 March 1979 and was refurbished in 2005.
facts.quote: It was designed by Sérgio Bernandes in 1973 and was inaugurated on 12 March 1979, being refurbished in 2005.

facts.fact: It was renamed in 1992 in honour of Ulysses Guimarães.
facts.quote: It was renamed in 1992 to honor Ulysses Guimarães.

facts.fact: It belongs to Brasília's Cultural Diffusion Sector on the Monumental Axis, with the Brasília Planetarium and the Brasília Choro Club.
facts.quote: The convention center is part of Brasílias Cultural Diffusion Sector, in the Monumental Axis, along with the Brasília Planetarium and the Brasília Choro Club.

facts.fact: It is split into three wings: west, south and north.
facts.quote: The convention center is split into three wings, the west wing, the south wing, and the north wing.

facts.fact: The west wing is Bernardes's original 1970s centre, with 2,000 m² of open ground floor and four auditoriums.
facts.quote: Comprising the area of the original Convention Center designed by Sérgio Bernardes in the 1970s, it has a free space of 2 thousand square meters on the ground and four auditoriums, named Alvorada, Planalto, Águas Claras and Buriti.

facts.fact: The south wing is a 10,200 m² air-conditioned hall for exhibitions and fairs.
facts.quote: An air-conditioned wing designed for exhibitions and fairs with 10,200 square meters.

facts.fact: The north wing holds the Master Auditorium for more than 3,000 people and 13 modular rooms.
facts.quote: In the North Wing, in addition to the Master Auditorium, with capacity for more than 3 thousand people, the wing has 13 modular rooms, a multipurpose area, dressing rooms, a VIP room and a press room.

facts.fact: Pacaembu Stadium is a football stadium in São Paulo's Pacaembu neighbourhood, owned by the city.
facts.quote: Located in the Pacaembu neighbourhood, it is owned by Municipal Prefecture of São Paulo.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 27 April 1940 in the presence of President Getúlio Vargas.
facts.quote: The stadium was inaugurated on 27 April 1940, in the presence of the Brazilian President Getúlio Vargas, the interventor Adhemar de Barros and the mayor of São Paulo, Prestes Maia.

facts.fact: It held 40,199 people on a pitch 104 m long and 70 m wide.
facts.quote: The stadium used to hold 40,199 people and its pitch dimensions are 104 m of length by 70 m of width, but is currently undergoing a renovation that will reduce capacity.

facts.fact: The state heritage council CONDEPHAAT listed it in 1998 for its Art Deco style, typical of its time.
facts.quote: The stadium was listed by the São Paulo state Council for the Defense of Historical, Archaeological, Artistic and Tourist Heritage (CONDEPHAAT) in 1998 due to its Art Deco style, characteristic of the period in which it was built.

facts.fact: Six matches of the 1950 FIFA World Cup were played there.
facts.quote: Six 1950 FIFA World Cup matches were played at Estádio do Pacaembu

facts.fact: The Museum of Football opened under the stadium's stands in 2008, covering 6,900 m².
facts.quote: The museum covers 6,900 square metres (1.7 acres), it was built at a cost of R$32.5 million, and is located below the stadium's bleachers.

facts.fact: It reopened on 27 January 2025 after a 40-month renovation, in which the south stand was replaced by a five-storey building.
facts.quote: On 27 January 2025, the stadium reopened to the public after a 40-month renovation. The most notable change to the stadium was with the demolition of the south stand, with a five-story building constructed in its place.

facts.fact: The Theatro Municipal is an opera house in the Centro district of Rio de Janeiro.
facts.quote: The Theatro Municipal ("Municipal Theater") is an opera house in the Centro district of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

facts.fact: Its eclectic design was inspired by Charles Garnier's Paris Opéra.
facts.quote: The building is designed in an eclectic style, inspired by the Paris Opéra of Charles Garnier.

facts.fact: The outside walls are inscribed with the names of classic European and Brazilian artists.
facts.quote: The outside walls are inscribed with the names of classic European and Brazilian artists.

facts.fact: It was conceived by Francisco de Oliveira Passos, son of the mayor, with Albert Guilbert.
facts.quote: Hence arose the opera venue, brainchild of Francisco de Oliveira Passos (Son of then mayor Francisco Pereira Passos) with the cooperation of Albert Guilbert and design inspired by the Paris Opera.

facts.fact: Building began in 1905 on a foundation of 1,180 wooden piles set in groundwater.
facts.quote: Building began in 1905 on a foundation of 1,180 wood poles rooted in groundwater.

facts.fact: Leading Brazilian painters and sculptors decorated it, and European craftsmen made its stained glass and mosaics.
facts.quote: To decorate the building, the most important Brazilian painters and sculptors of the time were summoned, such as Eliseu Visconti, Rodolfo Amoedo and the Bernardelli brothers, Henrique and Rodolfo. European artisans were also recruited to work on stained glasses and mosaic tiles.

facts.fact: It opened on 14 July 1909, after four and a half years of work, with seats for 1,739.
facts.quote: Finally, four and a half years later — a record time for the work that took the relay from 280 workers in two shifts — on July 14, 1909, President Nilo Peçanha inaugurated the Theatro Municipal do Rio de Janeiro, which had the capacity for 1,739 viewers.

facts.fact: Seating rose to 2,205 in 1934 and later to 2,361.
facts.quote: In 1934, upon the observation that the theater was small for the new size of the population of the city, auditory capacity was increased to 2,205 seats. The work, despite its complexity, was held in three months, record time for the season. Later, with some modifications, it acquired the current number of 2,361 places.

facts.fact: The Theatro da Paz is a theatre on Praça da República in Belém, built on Neoclassical lines during the Amazon rubber boom.
facts.quote: Theatro da Paz (Theater of Peace) is a theater located in the Praça da República (Republic Square) on the city of Belém, capital of the state of Pará, in Brazil. It was built following neoclassical architectural lines during the golden age of rubber in Amazon Basin.

facts.fact: Engineer José Tibúrcio Pereira Magalhães planned it, with some changes by the public works office.
facts.quote: Theatro da Paz was planned by engineer José Tibúrcio Pereira Magalhães, with some alterations added by the Public Constructions office.

facts.fact: Construction ran from 1869 to 1874, but it opened to the public only after an inquiry into its builders.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1869 and ended in 1874, but the theater was only opened to the public after an administrative investigation against its builders.

facts.fact: On each side, patios ringed by columns and staircases lead to Praça da República.
facts.quote: On each side, there are patios surrounded by columns and staircases giving access to Praça da República (Republic Square).

facts.fact: Italian painter Domenico de Angelis, who also decorated the Teatro Amazonas, planned its decoration and painted Greek gods on the auditorium ceiling.
facts.quote: Decoration was planned by Italian Domenico de Angelis who also decorated Teatro Amazonas in Manaus. He also painted the theater's panel in its spectacle room's roof, which depicted Greek gods, as well as the Jover roof, which was lost due to an infiltration and later restored in 1960 by another Italian artist, Armando Baloni.

facts.fact: Its façade has changed little over the years, apart from fewer columns over the main entrance; its architectural lines are unaltered.
facts.quote: Theatro da Paz has suffered minor alterations along the years to its façade, namely the reduction of the number of columns over the main entrance. Its architectural lines, however, remain unaltered.

facts.fact: A restoration in the 1990s brought back its original colours.
facts.quote: Theatro da Paz underwent another major reformation in the 90s, under governor Almir Gabriel, when its original colors were restored.

facts.fact: Brazil's heritage institute IPHAN listed it in 1963, and UNESCO named it a World Heritage Site in 2026.
facts.quote: It was listed as a historic structure by National Institute of Historic and Artistic Heritage (IPHAN) in 1963, and as a World Heritage Site by UNESCO in 2026.

facts.fact: Luz Station is a commuter and intercity rail station in São Paulo's Bom Retiro district.
facts.quote: Luz Station (Portuguese: Estação da Luz, IPA: [(i)staˈsɐ̃w dɐ ˈlus]) is a commuter rail and intercity rail station in the Bom Retiro district of São Paulo, Brazil, serving RFFSA, the intercity rail network of Brazil, CPTM Line 10-Turquoise, Line 11-Coral and Line 13-Jade (Airport Express).

facts.fact: British architect Charles Henry Driver designed it for the São Paulo Railway, and it was built between 1895 and 1901.
facts.quote: It is currently located in Bairro da Luz and was built between 1895 and 1901, designed by the British architect Charles Henry Driver for the São Paulo Railway, a company based in London that was responsible for building the first railway line in the state of São Paulo, connecting the port of Santos to the city of Jundiaí.

facts.fact: The station was built as the headquarters of the newly founded São Paulo Railway.
facts.quote: The station was built in the late 19th century with the purpose of being the headquarters of the newly founded São Paulo Railway.

facts.fact: The current building was finished in 1901 with materials brought from the UK.
facts.quote: The current building was finished in 1901. The materials for its construction were brought from UK.

facts.fact: It was made by Walter Macfarlane & Co.'s Saracen Foundry in Glasgow, assembled there, taken apart and shipped to São Paulo to be put together again.
facts.quote: The station was designed and produced by Walter Macfarlane & Co. Saracen Foundry, Glasgow. The station was assembled in Glasgow, then disassembled and sent to São Paulo where it was reassembled.

facts.fact: For many years its clock tower dominated the city skyline and set the city's clocks.
facts.quote: For many years, the station's clock tower dominated the city landscape, and for a time, served as the basis for clock adjustment in the city.

facts.fact: It houses the Museum of the Portuguese Language, opened in 2006.
facts.quote: The station houses the Museum of the Portuguese Language, established in 2006.

facts.fact: A major fire in 2015, starting in the museum, devastated the main building.
facts.quote: On 21 December 2015, the station suffered a major fire that started at the Museum of the Portuguese Language. The fire devastated the station's major building, and claimed one firefighter life. == Cultural influence == The station is a remnant from the period when the coffee was a major source of income to the city.

facts.fact: The station is protected as railway heritage, so it cannot be expanded.
facts.quote: The current Luz station is under railway heritage protection, meaning that it cannot be expanded in the future. === Touristic Express === Since 2009, Luz has been the terminus of the Touristic Express line, a touristic line that makes trips from Luz to Paranapiacaba and Jundiai.

facts.fact: The Mannerist church of São Bento in Rio de Janeiro is a primary example of Portuguese colonial architecture in the city and the country.
facts.quote: The Mannerist style church is a primary example of Portuguese colonial architecture in Rio and the country.

facts.fact: The abbey was founded in 1590 by Benedictine monks who came from Bahia.
facts.quote: The abbey was founded by Benedictine monks who came from the state of Bahia in 1590.

facts.fact: Its stone was quarried from the Morro da Viúva, and enslaved Africans did the building work.
facts.quote: African slaves provided the physical labor required to build the monastery. The stones used in its construction were mined from the Morro da Viúva (Widow's Hill), in the neighborhood of Flamengo.

facts.fact: Portuguese military engineer Francisco Frias de Mesquita drew up the plans and oversaw construction in 1617, drawing on the Mannerist style then popular in Portugal.
facts.quote: They also supervised a primary, secondary, and night school for adults. == Architecture == Portuguese military engineer, Francisco Frias de Mesquita, drew up the plans for the building and oversaw its construction in 1617. The Mannerist style, popular in Portugal at the time, provided the aesthetic inspiration for the structure.

facts.fact: Work on the church began in 1633, with a plan to finish in 1671; architect Bernardo de São Bento Correia de Souza changed the plans to include three naves.
facts.quote: Work on the church began in 1633, under the guidance of Abbott Francisco da Magdalena, with a plan to finish in 1671. The original plans were altered during construction by the architect Bernardo de São Bento Correia de Souza to include three naves.

facts.fact: The annex was completed only in 1755 with a convent designed by military engineer José Fernandes Pinto Alpoim.
facts.quote: The annex of the church was only completed in 1755, with the installation of a convent designed by military engineer José Fernandes Pinto Alpoim.

facts.fact: The Mannerist façade has three entrance arches under a triangular gable, flanked by two towers with pyramidal spires.
facts.quote: The façade was part of the original Mannerist project and featured a centralized edifice with three archways at the entrance, as well as a triangular gable. Two towers crowned by pyramidal spires flanked the entryway.

facts.fact: Set on a hilltop, it became a landmark for navigators.
facts.quote: Located on top of a hill, it became a point of reference for navigators.

facts.fact: The church interior is richly covered in gold-leaf gilding.
facts.quote: The interior of the church is ornately covered in gold leaf gilding, a style popularized during the Baroque period of the seventeenth century and the Rococo period of the eighteenth century.

facts.fact: The National Flag Memorial in Rosario is a monumental complex near the shore of the Paraná River.
facts.quote: The National Flag Memorial (Spanish, Monumento a la Bandera) in Rosario, Argentina, is a monumental complex built near the shore of the Paraná River.

facts.fact: It opened on 20 June 1957, the anniversary of the death of Manuel Belgrano, who created the Argentine flag and first raised it across the river in 1812.
facts.quote: It was inaugurated on June 20, 1957, the anniversary of the death of Manuel Belgrano, creator of the Argentine flag, who raised it for the first time on an island on the opposite shore of the river on February 27, 1812.

facts.fact: Alejandro Bustillo designed it in 1944 with fellow architect Ángel Guido.
facts.quote: Among Bustillo's best known later works was the National Flag Memorial in Rosario, designed in 1944 with fellow architect Ángel Guido and completed in 1957.

facts.fact: The complex covers about 10,000 m² and was built mostly of stone from the Andes, with sculptors José Fioravanti, Alfredo Bigatti and Eduardo Barnes.
facts.quote: The complex has a total area of about 10,000 square metres, and was built mostly using stone from the Andes, under the direction of architects Ángel Guido and Alejandro Bustillo, and the sculptors José Fioravanti, Alfredo Bigatti and Eduardo Barnes.

facts.fact: It has three parts: a 70-metre tower with Belgrano's crypt at its base, a Civic Courtyard for large open-air events, and a Triumphal Propylaeum.
facts.quote: The Monumento has three parts: the Tower (Torre) or mast, 70 metres high, which commemorates the Revolution of May 1810 and houses Manuel Belgrano's crypt in its base; the Civic Courtyard (Patio Cívico), which symbolizes the effort of the organization of the state (the Courtyard is used for massive open-air shows), and the Triumphal Propylaeum (Propileo Triunfal), representing the Nation as organized after the 1853 Constitution.

facts.fact: Under the Propylaeum is the Honour Room for the Flags of America, with the flags of every American nation.
facts.quote: Under the Propylaeum there is the Honour Room for the Flags of America (where the flags of all American nations are displayed).

facts.fact: The Propylaeum is reached by a pedestrian passage, Pasaje Juramento, from Plaza 25 de Mayo.
facts.quote: The Propylaeum can be accessed from the pedestrian passage called Pasaje Juramento ("Oath Passage"), which starts at Buenos Aires St. between the municipal building (Palacio de los Leones) and the Cathedral, in front of Plaza 25 de Mayo (May 25th Square).

facts.fact: The memorial and the park in front of it are the main site of Argentina's Flag Day celebrations on 20 June.
facts.quote: The Memorial and the National Flag Park located in front of it are the seat of the main celebrations of Flag Day on June 20.

facts.fact: The Usina del Arte is a cultural centre and auditorium in the former Don Pedro de Mendoza power plant in La Boca, Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: "The Arts Powerhouse") is a cultural centre and auditorium located on the former Don Pedro de Mendoza Power Plant ("usina" in Spanish) at La Boca neighborhood, Buenos Aires.

facts.fact: Italian architect Juan (Giovanni) Chiogna designed it as a power plant for the Italo-Argentine Electricity Company; it was built by Martignone and Sons between 1912 and 1916.
facts.quote: The building was designed by the Italian architect Juan Chiogna to house a power plant of the Italo-Argentine Electricity Company (Compañía Italo-Argentina de Electricidad, abbrevriated "CIAE") and built by the company Martignone and Sons between 1912 and 1916, when it was inaugurated.

facts.fact: The plant supplied the city with electricity for about 80 years until the service was nationalised in the 1990s, then was abandoned and decayed.
facts.quote: For the next 80 years it worked providing electricity to the city, until the service was nationalized in the 1990s. The building was later abandoned by the state company and fell into disrepair.

facts.fact: After decades of neglect the city refurbished it as a cultural centre, reopened in May 2012 with a 1,200-seat symphonic auditorium.
facts.quote: After being abandoned through decades, the government of the city of Buenos Aires refurbished the building to become a cultural center, being reopened in May 2012 with the inauguration of a symphonic auditorium with capacity for 1,200 people.

facts.fact: Its Italianate late-Gothic or early-Renaissance style and its clock tower, seen from afar, have been called an almost exact copy of Florence's Palazzo della Signoria.
facts.quote: The building stands out for its distinctive Italianate late Gothic or early Renacentist architecture and its clock tower which can be seen from a distance, especially from the La Plata freeway that today bestrides it, "an almost exact reproduction of the Florentine Palazzo Della Signoria".

facts.fact: Inside are large former generator halls with iron truss roofs covered in zinc sheet.
facts.quote: The interiors are large rooms that were used for electric generators, with iron truss roofs and a zinc sheet roof.

facts.fact: Its battlemented square tower, clock, gargoyles, round arches and exposed brick are features Chiogna used in all his buildings for the electricity company.
facts.quote: The square tower with battlements, the inclusion of the clock, the use of gargoyles and semicircular arches with the addition of the exposed bricks and plaster elements imitating stone blocks that the Pedro de Mendoza Powerhouse shows on its exterior summarize just some of the characteristics that Chiogna used in all the works carried out for the CIAE and almost simultaneously with the completion of this one.

facts.fact: The Legislative Palace in Montevideo's Aguada neighbourhood is the seat of Uruguay's General Assembly.
facts.quote: The Legislative Palace of Uruguay (Spanish: Palacio Legislativo del Uruguay) is a monumental building, meeting place of the General Assembly of Uruguay, and the seat of the legislative branch of the Uruguayan government. It is located in the Aguada neighborhood of Montevideo.

facts.fact: Built between 1904 and 1925, it opened on 25 August 1925, the centenary of the Declaration of Independence.
facts.quote: Constructed between 1904 and 1925, the building was inaugurated on August 25, 1925, in commemoration of the centenary of the Declaration of Independence.

facts.fact: Vittorio Meano, then building Argentina's Congress Palace, won the 1904 international competition, but died before learning he had won.
facts.quote: The project of the architect Vittorio Meano, who at that time was building the Palace of the Argentine National Congress in Buenos Aires, was approved. He never found out that his project had been the winner since he died suddenly before he could be contacted by the Legislative Palace Commission, organizer of the project competition.

facts.fact: It was designed by Italian architects Vittorio Meano and Gaetano Moretti, who planned the marble-clad interior.
