facts.quote: It was designed by Italian architects Vittorio Meano and Gaetano Moretti, who planned the building's interior that is covered with marble.

facts.fact: It is an eclectic Greco-Roman building whose façades, walls, vaults and columns are covered with Uruguayan marbles.
facts.quote: The inauguration was presided over by President José Serrato. == Architecture == The palace is a Greco-Roman eclecticist-styled building whose facades, interior walls, vaults and columns are covered with different marbles from Uruguay.

facts.fact: The main façade lines up with the axis of Libertador Avenue.
facts.quote: The main facade of the building is aligned with the axis of symmetry of Libertador Avenue.

facts.fact: At its centre, the Hall of the Lost Steps, inspired by Renaissance cathedrals, has two vaults and a central skylight and separates the Senate and House chambers.
facts.quote: In the nave of the building is the Hall of the Lost Steps (Spanish: Salón de los Pasos Perdidos), which is inspired by the cathedrals of the Renaissance and is composed of two vaults and a central skylight, which separates the two chambers in which the Senate and the House of Representatives meet.

facts.fact: It was declared a National Historic Monument in 1975.
facts.quote: It was declared a National Historic Monument in 1975 by the government of President Juan María Bordaberry.

facts.fact: Retiro bus station is the main bus terminal of Buenos Aires, two blocks north of Retiro railway station.
facts.quote: Retiro bus station (Spanish: Terminal de Ómnibus de Retiro) is the main bus terminal in Buenos Aires, Argentina. It is situated in the Retiro district, two blocks north of Retiro railway station. == Overview == The station was commissioned in 1980 by the municipal government under Mayor Osvaldo Cacciatore.

facts.fact: The city government under Mayor Osvaldo Cacciatore commissioned it in 1980.
facts.quote: The station was commissioned in 1980 by the municipal government under Mayor Osvaldo Cacciatore.

facts.fact: Designed by Fernando Serra, Jorge Valera and Raúl Petrucci, it opened in 1983.
facts.quote: Designed by Fernando Serra, Jorge Valera, and Raúl Petrucci, the station was inaugurated in 1983.

facts.fact: The station is nearly 400 metres long, with 75 gates, and five raised walkways lead to it from the car park.
facts.quote: The station, nearly 400 metres (440 yd) in length, includes 75 gates and is accessible from the parking lot via five elevated walkways.

facts.fact: Buses leave from it for all of Argentina and for neighbouring countries.
facts.quote: Buses depart from Retiro for all parts of Argentina, and for the neighbouring countries of Uruguay, Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, and Chile, as well as for Lima, Peru.

facts.fact: A private company, Teba S.A., has run it since 1993.
facts.quote: The bus station has been operated since 1993 by Teba S.A., a private company.

facts.fact: Torre Espacial, or Torre Interama, is a 200-metre observation tower in the Villa Soldati area of Buenos Aires.
facts.quote: Torre Espacial, or Torre Interama, is a 200 metres (660 ft) high observation tower in the Villa Soldati section of Buenos Aires, Argentina.

facts.fact: The Austrian firm Waagner-Biro designed and made the tower, built from 1980 to May 1981 for the Parque de la Ciudad amusement park.
facts.quote: The tower was designed and manufactured in Austria by Waagner-Biro, and built between 1980 and May 1981 for the Parque de la Ciudad amusement park.

facts.fact: The park developer's bankruptcy delayed it, and it opened to the public on 9 July 1985.
facts.quote: The bankruptcy of the amusement park's developer, Interama S.A., delayed delivery of the observation tower components; the tower was finally opened to the public on July 9, 1985.

facts.fact: Its observation decks are at 120, 124 and 176 metres; from the top one the coast of Uruguay can be seen.
facts.quote: It features observation decks at 120, 124, and 176 meters; from the highest deck it is possible to see the Uruguay coast.

facts.fact: It was declared a City Cultural Landmark in 2010.
facts.quote: The Torre Espacial was declared a City Cultural Landmark on November 22, 2010.

facts.fact: Closed in 2003, it reopened after renovation in November 2011.
facts.quote: It was closed in 2003 but following renovation works was reopened on November 26, 2011.

facts.fact: The Palace of Justice in Buenos Aires is the seat of Argentina's Supreme Court and other lower courts.
facts.quote: It is the seat of the Supreme Court and other lower courts.

facts.fact: French architect Norbert Maillart designed the original building in 1889, but the Baring crisis of 1890 held up construction for almost 20 years.
facts.quote: The original building was designed by French architect Norbert Maillart in 1889, during the presidency of Miguel Juárez Celman, but the Baring crisis of 1890 paralyzed the start of construction for almost 20 years.

facts.fact: Built in a monumental eclectic Neoclassical style, it has a total floor area of 60,100 m².
facts.quote: Designed in a monumental Eclectic neoclassical style and constructed between 1905 and 1910, the building is a National Historic Landmark and has a total floor area of 60,100 m2 (647,000 sq ft).

facts.fact: Part of it opened in 1910 for the centenary of the May Revolution.
facts.quote: A part of the Palace of Justice was inaugurated in 1910 by President José Figueroa Alcorta, during the celebrations for the Centennial of the May Revolution.

facts.fact: Around 1925 the original mansard top was replaced by an extra floor to give the growing courts more space.
facts.quote: Around 1925, the original project was modified due to the growth of the Judicial Branch, in such a way that the original top of the building, which included a mansard, gave way to one more floor, gaining the necessary surface area.

facts.fact: The palace was not finished until 1942, and was declared a National Historic Monument in 1999.
facts.quote: The palace would not be finished until 1942. It was declared National Historic Monument of Argentina in 1999 via decree 349.

facts.fact: Its façades are covered in imitation Paris stone.
facts.quote: Its facades are covered in imitation Paris stone.

facts.fact: Architect Virginio Colombo came from Milan to design the many ornaments on the façade.
facts.quote: To design the numerous ornaments on the façade, the architect Virginio Colombo arrived from Milan, and he would end up settling in Buenos Aires and becoming a major representative of the art nouveau movement in local architecture. == In popular culture == Many movies have been filmed inside the palace, including: == References ==

facts.fact: The Hotel Casino Carrasco is a historic hotel and casino in Montevideo.
facts.quote: The Hotel Casino Carrasco is a historic five star hotel and casino in Montevideo, Uruguay.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1912, led by architects Gastón Mallet and the Swiss Jacques Dunant.
facts.quote: The construction of the hotel began in 1912, under the leadership and projection of the architects Gastón Mallet and the Swiss Jacques Dunant.

facts.fact: The First World War halted the works for nine years; the city bought the unfinished building and opened it on 29 January 1921.
facts.quote: The outbreak of the World War I forced the suspension of construction works for nine years. Later, the Municipality of Montevideo bought the land and the monumental unfinished building, to continue the works and finally inaugurate them, on January 29, 1921.

facts.fact: It became a landmark of luxury and hosted guests such as Albert Einstein in 1925 and Federico García Lorca in 1934.
facts.quote: It soon became a landmark of luxury for tourists visiting the city, and many lodged many famous personalities, such as Albert Einstein (1925) and Federico García Lorca (1934).

facts.fact: It was declared National Historical Heritage in 1975.
facts.quote: In 1975 it was declared a National Historical Heritage.

facts.fact: It closed in 1997; renovation began in 2009 and was completed in 2013.
facts.quote: In 1997 it closed its doors. Renovation work began in 2009 by the company Carrasco Nobile Sociedad Anónima, and culminated in 2013.

facts.fact: On Montevideo's Rambla, it is the centre of the Carrasco district plan drawn by landscape architects Charles Thays and Edouard André.
facts.quote: Located on the Rambla of Montevideo, the hotel stands as the center of the urban plan designed for the barrio Carrasco, in the first decades of the 20th century, by the French landscape architects Charles Thays and Edouard André.

facts.fact: Its eclectic, historicist style is mainly Neoclassical and Baroque, inspired by European palace hotels.
facts.quote: Its architectural style is eclectic-historicist with a predominance of neoclassical and baroque and inspired by European palace hotels.

facts.fact: The Museum of Memory and Human Rights in Santiago commemorates victims of human rights violations under Augusto Pinochet's dictatorship, 1973–1990.
facts.quote: The Museum of Memory and Human Rights (in Spanish: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos) is a museum in Santiago, Chile, which commemorates the victims of human rights violations during the military dictatorship led by Augusto Pinochet between 1973 and 1990.

facts.fact: President Michelle Bachelet announced the museum in May 2007 and, a month later, a public competition for its architectural design.
facts.quote: In her speech on May 21, 2007, before the full Congress, President Michelle Bachelet announced the construction of a memorial museum, and a month later she announced a public competition to select an architectural design for it.

facts.fact: The competition was won by Estudio America, a group of Brazilian architects based in São Paulo.
facts.quote: On August 28 of that year, it was announced that the winning project belonged to a group of Brazilian architects from the office "Estudio America", located in São Paulo.

facts.fact: Bachelet laid the first stone on 10 December 2008.
facts.quote: The first stone of the museum was laid on December 10, 2008, by Bachelet, who was herself a victim of torture during the dictatorship of Pinochet.

facts.fact: It opened on 11 January 2010 as part of Chile's bicentennial.
facts.quote: It was inaugurated by then-president Michelle Bachelet on January 11, 2010, as part of government's commemoration of the bicentennial of Chile. == History == In her speech on May 21, 2007, before the full Congress, President Michelle Bachelet announced the construction of a memorial museum, and a month later she announced a public competition to select an architectural design for it.

facts.fact: It displays torture devices, prisoners' letters, press cuttings and survivors' testimony.
facts.quote: The museum houses torture devices used during the Pinochet dictatorship, letters to family members by prisoners in detention centers, newspaper clippings, and testimony from survivors.

facts.fact: Víctor Jara's last poem, written during the 1973 coup, runs across the museum's entrance.
facts.quote: Chilean popular icon and folksinger Víctor Jara's last poem, Estadio Chile, written shortly before his death in the stadium during the 1973 coup, sprawls across the entrance to the museum.

facts.fact: The Teatro del Lago is a theatre and concert hall in Frutillar, Chile, on the shore of Lake Llanquihue.
facts.quote: The Teatro del Lago (Theatre of the Lake) is a stage theatre and concert hall located in Frutillar, Los Lagos Region, Chile. == Overview == Housed in a 10,000 m2 building, and located on the shores of Llanquihue Lake, the Teatro del Lago includes the 1,178 capacity Espacio Volcán Tronador – Sala Nestlé concert hall; an amphitheater, seating 270, and a range of other multipurpose salons and foyers, exhibition areas, rehearsal spaces, conference rooms and congress halls.

facts.fact: Its 10,000 m² building holds a 1,178-seat concert hall, a 270-seat amphitheatre, rehearsal spaces and conference rooms.
facts.quote: Housed in a 10,000 m2 building, and located on the shores of Llanquihue Lake, the Teatro del Lago includes the 1,178 capacity Espacio Volcán Tronador – Sala Nestlé concert hall; an amphitheater, seating 270, and a range of other multipurpose salons and foyers, exhibition areas, rehearsal spaces, conference rooms and congress halls.

facts.fact: It was built as a new home for the Semanas Musicales de Frutillar festival after the Hotel Frutillar burned down in 1996.
facts.quote: The construction of the theater to create a new cultural space to house the Semanas Musicals de Frutillar after the Hotel Frutillar burned down in 1996.

facts.fact: Architects Gerardo Köster and Gustavo Greene began building it on 27 January 1998, funded by businessman Guillermo Schiess.
facts.quote: Architects Geradro Köster and Gustavo Greene began construction on January 27, 1998 with financial support from Schiess.

facts.fact: In 2008 architects from Amercanda (Bernd Haller, Cristián Valdés, Pablo Cordua and Andrés Alvear) joined the project to build with better acoustic materials.
facts.quote: In 2008 a new set of architects from Amercanda - Bernd Haller, Cristián Valdés, Pablo Cordua y Andrés Alvear - were added to the project to build with better acoustic materials.

facts.fact: It opened on 6 November 2010 after twelve years of work, at a cost of US$20 million.
facts.quote: After twelve years of work, the theater opened on November 6, 2010 at a cost of $20 million (US).

facts.fact: It was one of the largest concert spaces opened in Chile since the 1950s.
facts.quote: It immediately became one of the largest concert spaces ever opened in Chile since the 1950s. == References == == External links == Teatro del Lago website (in Spanish) Semanas Musicales website (in Spanish)

facts.fact: Estación Mapocho is a former railway station in Santiago, used as a cultural centre since 1994.
facts.quote: Estación Mapocho is a former railway station that has been refitted as a cultural center since 1994, hosting a variety of events in Santiago, Chile.

facts.fact: Its design and construction began in 1905 under Emilio Jecquier, a Chilean architect based in France.
facts.quote: The design and construction of the station began in 1905 at the hands of Emilio Jecquier, a Chilean architect based in France.

facts.fact: The 280-metre-long, 17-metre-high structure has a masonry base and a steel vault once glazed, now clad in copper; its steelwork was built by the Belgian firm Haine Saint Pierre.
facts.quote: The 280-metre-long, 17-metre-high structure was composed of a base of masonry and a steel vault covered in glass (now copper). The steel structure was constructed by the Belgian company Haine Saint Pierre.

facts.fact: It was inaugurated on 12 May 1912 and opened to the public in 1913.
facts.quote: The official inauguration of the station took place on May 12, 1912, and the station opened to the public in 1913.

facts.fact: It was one of several works built to mark the centenary of Chilean independence.
facts.quote: The station was one of several civil works commissioned to celebrate the first centenary of Chilean independence, along with the park of Santa Lucía Hill, the Chilean High Court of Justice, and the Chilean National Museum of Fine Arts.

facts.fact: It stands on the south bank of the Mapocho River, near the Mercado Central.
facts.quote: The building is located at the intersection of two streets, Presidente Balmaceda and Bandera, on the south bank of the Mapocho River close to the Mercado Central de Santiago.

facts.fact: It was declared a National Monument in 1976 for its imposing architecture and historic value.
facts.quote: In recognition of its imposing architecture and its sentimental and historic value, the building was declared a National Monument by law in 1976.

facts.fact: Architects Montserrat Palmer, Teodoro Fernández, Ramón López and Rodrigo Pérez de Arce remodelled its 10,000 m² with minimal change, preserving the original work wherever possible.
facts.quote: Architects Montserrat Palmer, Teodoro Fernández, Ramón López and Rodrigo Pérez de Arce were appointed to carry out the remodeling work. Their proposal involved remodeling the 10,000 square metre space with minimal alteration or disruption, preserving the original work of architect wherever possible.

facts.fact: The restoration won the Reina Sofía International Award for Conservation and Restoration of Cultural Heritage in 2008.
facts.quote: It also received the Reina Sofía International Award for Conservation and Restoration of Cultural Heritage in 2008.

facts.fact: The Teatro Municipal is Santiago's most important theatre and opera house, home of the National Opera of Chile.
facts.quote: The Teatro Municipal, National Opera of Chile is the most important stage theatre and opera house in Santiago, Chile.

facts.fact: Claudio Brunet des Baines gave it a French Neoclassical exterior; after his death in 1855, Lucien Hénault took over the design.
facts.quote: Brunet des Baines created a French Neoclassical exterior for the theater, though his 1855 death left the supervision of the design to his countryman, Lucien Hénault, and to the latter's assistant, Manuel Aldunate.

facts.fact: The design team also worked with Charles Garnier, architect of the Paris Opéra.
facts.quote: The new team also benefited from a collaboration with Charles Garnier, the architect of the Opéra National de Paris.

facts.fact: It opened on 17 September 1857 with Verdi's Ernani, seating 1,800.
facts.quote: The Teatro Municipal was inaugurated on September 17, 1857, with the opera Ernani by Giuseppe Verdi, performed by an Italian company brought in specially for the occasion. At the time, the theatre held 1,800 spectators, and included distinctive interior details such as a teardrop crystal chandelier.

facts.fact: A fire after a performance on 8 December 1870 nearly destroyed it; it was rebuilt to Hénault's design and completed on 16 July 1873.
facts.quote: A December 8, 1870, performance by opera diva Carlotta Patti was followed by a massive fire, which practically destroyed the building. A quick response by both the local government and Chilean high society resulted in the theatre's prompt reconstruction, designed by Henault and completed on July 16, 1873.

facts.fact: It survived the 1906 earthquake, which destroyed most of its interior, and a second fire in 1927.
facts.quote: The theatre went through a devastating 1906 earthquake, suffering the loss of most of its interior, and a second, serious fire in 1927, although it recovered quickly on both occasions.

facts.fact: After these rebuilds the main hall held 1,500, with a more opulent interior.
facts.quote: Following these reconstructions, the theatre's capacity was reduced to 1,500 in the main hall; however, its interior became more opulent.

facts.fact: It was declared a National Monument in 1974.
facts.quote: The Teatro Municipal was declared a National Monument, in 1974.

facts.fact: La Moneda Palace is the seat of the president of Chile.
facts.quote: La Moneda Palace (Spanish: Palacio de La Moneda, pronounced [paˈlasjo ðe la moˈneða], lit: Palace of the Mint), or simply La Moneda, is the seat of the president of the Republic of Chile.

facts.fact: It began as the colonial mint, designed by the Italian architect Joaquín Toesca; construction began in 1784 and it opened in 1805.
facts.quote: La Moneda was the colonial mint house of the city during colonial times, and was designed by the Italian architect Joaquín Toesca. Construction began in 1784 and it was opened in 1805.

facts.fact: Materials came from around Chile and abroad: limestone, river sand, red and white stone from Santiago's hills, oak and cypress from Valdivia and Spanish metalwork.
facts.quote: Works on the building started in 1784, with building materials arriving the following year from around Chile and the world: limestone from the Polpaico country estate; sand from the Maipo River; red stones from a quarry at the Cerro San Cristóbal in Santiago; white stone from the neighbouring Cerro Blanco; oak and cypress wood from Valdivia; Spanish metal works from Vizcaya.

facts.fact: Twenty kinds of brick were baked in Santiago for lintels, corners, floors, mouldings and solid walls more than a metre thick.
facts.quote: Twenty varieties of brick were baked in Santiago for the construction of lintels, comers, floors, moldings, and of the solid walls more than a meter thick.

facts.fact: Toesca died in 1799 and military engineer Agustín Cavallero finished the work.
facts.quote: Toesca died in 1799, before seeing his work finished, and military engineer Agustin Cavallero took over the project.

facts.fact: It is built in a pure Neoclassical style with Roman Doric influences.
facts.quote: The Palacio de la Moneda is built in a pure neoclassical style with Roman Doric influences.

facts.fact: Its rooms are laid out along cross axes around several patios, including the Patio de los Naranjos used for presidential ceremonies.
facts.quote: Its main façade faces Moneda street, and its rooms are distributed along the transverse and longitudinal axes forming several patios. Behind this façade lie three patios: the Patio de los Cañones, which functions as an entrance hall; a covered patio; and finally the Patio de los Naranjos, where presidential ceremonies take place.

facts.fact: The Chilean Air Force attacked the palace with rockets and cannon fire in the coup of 11 September 1973.
facts.quote: During the military coup d'état on September 11, 1973, the Chilean Air Force strafed the palace with unguided rockets and automatic cannon fire.

facts.fact: Repairs were completed in March 1981, though some bullet marks were kept and can still be seen.
facts.quote: Restoration projects of the damage caused were completed in March 1981, although some bullet marks have been preserved and can still be seen today.

facts.fact: The Rafael Uribe Uribe Palace of Culture is a public building in Medellín that hosts cultural programmes of the Department of Antioquia.
facts.quote: The Rafael Uribe Uribe Palace of Culture is a public building in Medellín, that houses cultural programs related to the Department of Antioquia, such as concerts, conferences, and art exhibitions.

facts.fact: It was built from 1925 to 1937 as the seat of the Antioquia government, to a Gothic Revival design by Belgian architect Agustín Goovaerts.
facts.quote: It was under construction from the 1925 to 1937 and designed by Belgian architect Agustín Goovaerts in a Gothic Revival style.

facts.fact: A second building stage added the octagonal block, the east wing and the stairs with their hallways and balconies on Bolívar Street.
facts.quote: This construction stage involved the construction of the octagonal unit and the East Wing and the stairs with their hallways and balconies on Bolívar Street.

facts.fact: Architects Gerardo Mejía, Gustavo Restrepo and Gustavo Aristizabal were hired to finish it; they built the north façade and brought back some original decoration.
facts.quote: The architects Gerardo Mejía, Gustavo Restrepo, and Gustavo Aristizabal were contracted to finish the construction. They led the construction of the north facade and regained some elements of the original decoration.

facts.fact: The palace has four floors, a central courtyard and a rooftop lookout.
facts.quote: The Palace has four floors, a center courtyard and rooftop observation area.

facts.fact: The dome's metal supports were imported from Belgium in 1928 and assembled without welding, using red-hot bolts as in New York skyscrapers.
facts.quote: The metal supports were imported from Belgium in 1928 and their assembly was done according to the model used for the New York skyscrapers, heating the nuts and bolts until incandescent with a tightening effect, and giving strength to the structure despite the absence of welding. == Gallery == == References == == External links == Institute of Culture and Heritage of Antioquia

facts.fact: The large dome now serves as an auditorium and projection room.
facts.quote: The large dome located in the building is also used as an auditorium and a projection room, and can be used to watch movies. == Location == It is located in the La Candelaria commune, in the central-eastern zone of Medellín.

facts.fact: It was made a national monument of Colombia in 1982.
facts.quote: Finally, in 1982, under the resolution 000002 of the National Council of National Monuments, the Palace was upgraded to a national monument.

facts.fact: San Javier Library, officially the Father José Luis Arroyave Restrepo Library, is one of ten library parks in Medellín, named for the San Javier district.
facts.quote: Father José Luis Arroyave Restrepo Library, most commonly known as San Javier Library (Spanish: Parque Biblioteca San Javier) for its location in the San Javier commune, is one of ten library parks in Medellín, Colombia.

facts.fact: It was designed by architect Javier Vera.
facts.quote: The library was designed by architect Javier Vera.

facts.fact: It sits on a hillside south of the San Javier metro station.
facts.quote: A hillside area south of the San Javier metro station was chosen as the site of the San Javier Library Park.

facts.fact: It stands at the start of the San Cristóbal Metrocable line.
facts.quote: It is located at the beginning of the San Cristobal Metro Cable.

facts.fact: Construction began on 1 June 2005.
facts.quote: Construction began on June 1, 2005.

facts.fact: The León de Greiff Public Library (Biblioteca La Ladera) in Medellín is among the works of Giancarlo Mazzanti, with the Biblioteca Parque España.
facts.quote: Mazzanti's work includes the Biblioteca Parque España, the León de Greiff Public Library (Bibliotheca La Ladera) in Medellín, the Gerardo Molina Public School, the Nazca Restaurant, Habitar 72, Habitar 74, and the Medellin Coliseum (for the IX South American Games).

facts.fact: The National Capitol stands on Plaza de Bolívar in central Bogotá; building began in 1848 and was finished in 1926.
facts.quote: The National Capitol of Colombia (Spanish: Capitolio Nacional de Colombia), often simply referred to as Capitolio Nacional (National Capitol), is a building on Plaza de Bolívar in central Bogotá, the construction of which began in 1848 and was finished in 1926.

facts.fact: It houses both chambers of the Congress of Colombia.
facts.quote: It houses both houses of the Congress of Colombia.

facts.fact: It was designed by Thomas Reed.
facts.quote: It was designed by Thomas Reed.

facts.fact: Reed was a Danish architect born on Saint Croix, who studied in Germany and England and reached New Granada in 1847.
facts.quote: Thomas Reed (1817–1878), was a Danish architect born in the 19th century in the Saint Croix Island (at the time when it was a dependent territory of the Kingdom of Denmark). He studied in Germany and England, and arrived in the Republic of New Granada in 1847.

facts.fact: President Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera hired Reed to build the Capitol.
facts.quote: In Bogotá he was contracted to build the New Granada National Capitol by the president Tomás Cipriano de Mosquera.

facts.fact: In 1938 Ignacio Gómez Jaramillo painted two murals for the Capitol.
facts.quote: In 1938, Ignacio Gómez Jaramillo painted two murals for the Capitolio Nacional in Bogotá.

facts.fact: Santiago Martínez Delgado's 1947 fresco in the elliptical chamber, showing Bolívar and Santander leaving the Cúcuta congress, is considered the most important fresco in the country.
facts.quote: This mural of the Elliptic chamber National Congress Building, made in the fresco style, represents Simón Bolivar and Santander exiting the Cucuta congress during the creation of Gran Colombia. The mural is considered the most important fresco in the country and the artist's main masterpiece. == References == == External links == Media related to Capitolio Nacional de Colombia at Wikimedia Commons

facts.fact: The National Library of Venezuela in Caracas is the country's legal deposit library.
facts.quote: The Biblioteca Nacional de Venezuela (in English: National Library of Venezuela), located in Caracas, is the legal deposit and copyright for Venezuela.

facts.fact: The library was founded on 13 July 1833 by decree of General José Antonio Páez.
facts.quote: It was established on July 13, 1833, by decree of General José Antonio Páez.

facts.fact: Its current headquarters was designed by Tomás Sanabria between 1981 and 1989 in the Brutalist style.
facts.quote: The current headquarters of the library was designed by architect Tomás Sanabria from 1981 to 1989 in the style of Brutalist architecture, featuring a range of design elements and distinctive construction techniques.

facts.fact: Centro Financiero Confinanzas, known as Torre de David, is an unfinished, abandoned skyscraper in Caracas.
facts.quote: Centro Financiero Confinanzas (English: Confinanzas Financial Center), also known as Torre de David (the Tower of David) is an unfinished abandoned skyscraper in Caracas, the capital of Venezuela.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1990 and stopped in 1994 because of the Venezuelan banking crisis.
facts.quote: The construction of the tower began in 1990 but was halted in 1994 due to the Venezuelan banking crisis.

facts.fact: The tower takes its nickname from its main investor, David Brillembourg, who died in 1993.
facts.quote: This tower in downtown Caracas is nicknamed "Torre de David" after David Brillembourg, the tower's main investor who died from cancer in 1993.

facts.fact: The complex has six buildings, including the 171 m, 45-storey Torre A with a heliport, and 12 floors of parking.
facts.quote: The complex has six buildings: El Atrio (a lobby and conference room), Torre A that is 171m tall (equaling 45 stories) and includes a heliport, Torre B, Edificio K, Edificio Z, and 12 floors of parking.

facts.fact: The building has no elevators, electricity, running water or, in many places, walls.
facts.quote: The building lacks elevators, installed electricity, running water, balcony railing, windows, and even walls in many places.

facts.fact: Squatters occupied the tower from October 2007, starting with over 200 families.
facts.quote: The housing shortage led to occupation of the complex by squatters led by ex-convicts in October 2007, with over 200 families, representing about 40% of Caracas's "informal communities", taking over the center.

facts.fact: By June 2015 all of the residents had been moved to new homes.
facts.quote: By June 2015, all of the residents were relocated to their new homes.

facts.fact: Torre David, a documentary by Urban Think Tank, won a Golden Lion at the 2012 Venice Architecture Biennale.
facts.quote: Torre David, a documentary by Urban Think Tank, won a Golden Lion at the 2012 Venice Architecture Biennale.

facts.fact: The Palacio Federal Legislativo in Caracas houses Venezuela's National Assembly.
facts.quote: The Palacio Federal Legislativo (English: Federal Legislative Palace), also known as the Capitolio, is a historic building in Caracas, Venezuela, which houses the National Assembly.

facts.fact: It was built between 1872 and 1877 under President Antonio Guzmán Blanco, to a design by Luciano Urdaneta Vargas.
facts.quote: Located southwest of the Plaza Bolívar, it was built between 1872 and 1877 by President Antonio Guzmán Blanco to a design by the architect Luciano Urdaneta Vargas.

facts.fact: The building uses structural cast iron and replaced a convent on the site.
facts.quote: The Palacio Federal Legislativo, located to the west of Plaza Bolívar, incorporates structural cast iron. It replaced a convent on the site.

facts.fact: Painted bright white, it has a gilded oval dome over an elliptical room known as the Oval Room.
facts.quote: The building is painted bright white and has a gilded oval-shaped dome crowning an elliptically shaped room (known as the Oval Room).

facts.fact: The dome's ceiling carries Martín Tovar y Tovar's painting of the Battle of Carabobo.
facts.quote: The dome's ceiling has a painting by Martín Tovar y Tovar which vividly depicts the crucial Battle of Carabobo in the Venezuelan War of Independence against Spanish colonial rule.

facts.fact: The complex is two rectangular volumes joined by two lower sections around a courtyard with a central fountain.
facts.quote: The complex consists of two rectangular volumes connected by two lower sections. It encloses a courtyard with a central fountain set in a small garden inside iron railings.

facts.fact: The Legislative Palace's facade, completed in 1877, is symmetrical with a central portico.
facts.quote: The façade of the Legislative Palace, completed in 1877, is symmetrical in design. It has a portico at the center.

facts.fact: The middle one of its three columned portals has two caryatids representing Justice and Freedom.
facts.quote: There are three columnated portals, the one in the centre presenting two caryatids representing Justice and Freedom.

facts.fact: The complex has been a National Historic Monument since 22 August 1997.
facts.quote: The complex has been a National Historic Monument since 22 August 1997.

facts.fact: The Supreme Court has worked from its building in New Delhi since 1958.
facts.quote: It has operated from the Supreme Court building in New Delhi since 1958.

facts.fact: The building is shaped to symbolise the scales of justice, with a central wing between two side wings.
facts.quote: The court building is shaped to symbolise the scales of justice with a central wing flanked by a wing on either side.

facts.fact: The central wing holds the chief justice's court, the largest courtroom, under a 27.6 m dome with a colonnaded verandah.
facts.quote: The central wing consists of the chief justice's court, the largest of the courtrooms, flanked by two court halls on either side. It has a 27.6 m (91 ft) high dome and a spacious colonnaded verandah.

facts.fact: The main block stands on a triangular 17-acre plot.
facts.quote: The main block of the building was built on a triangular plot of land measuring 17 acres (6.9 ha).

facts.fact: It was designed in the Indo-British style by Ganesh Bhikaji Deolalikar, the first Indian to head the Central Public Works Department.
facts.quote: It is designed in the Indo-British architectural style by Ganesh Bhikaji Deolalikar, the first Indian to head the Central Public Works Department.

facts.fact: The scales-of-justice design was made to fit the triangular site.
facts.quote: The design of scales of justice was to conform to this triangular site and according to Prasad was the conception of justice for Indians.

facts.fact: Two wings were added in 1979 and extended in 1994.
facts.quote: In 1979, two wings were added to the complex, and they were further extended in 1994.

facts.fact: The building has 15 courtrooms.
facts.quote: There are 15 courtrooms located in various parts of the building.

facts.fact: The stadium was first built by the Government of India for the 1982 Asian Games.
facts.quote: The Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium was constructed by the Government of India to host the 1982 Asian Games.

facts.fact: It was redesigned by the German firms Gerkan, Marg and Partners and Schlaich Bergermann Partner.
facts.quote: The stadium was redesigned by the German architectural companies Gerkan, Marg and Partners and Schlaich Bergermann Partner.

facts.fact: Renovation started in 2007 and the remodelled stadium opened on 27 July 2010.
facts.quote: Renovation of the stadium started in 2007. Nearly 4,000 construction workers worked on the stadium in double shifts. The substantially remodelled and modernised stadium was inaugurated on 27 July 2010.

facts.fact: The renovation cut the capacity from 78,000 to 60,254 seats.
facts.quote: The capacity of the stadium was reduced from 78,000 to 60,254.

facts.fact: The 53,800 m2 Teflon-coated roof was designed by Schlaich Bergermann Partner.
facts.quote: The 53,800 m2 (579,000 sq ft) Teflon-coated roof, designed by the German structural engineering and consulting firm Schlaich Bergermann Partner, was built at a cost of ₹308 crore (US$67.36 million).

facts.fact: The roof is PTFE glass-fibre fabric, one of the largest membrane roofs in the world.
facts.quote: Taiyo Membrane Corporation supplied and installed the PTFE glass fibre fabric roof. It is one of the largest membrane roof system in the world.

facts.fact: The roof and its supports used 8,500 tonnes of steel.
facts.quote: 8,500 tonnes of steel were used in the construction of the stadium's roof and its support structure.

facts.fact: Its design is similar to the Century Lotus Stadium in Foshan, China, by the same firm.
facts.quote: The design of the stadium is similar to Century Lotus Stadium in Foshan, China, designed by the same company.

facts.fact: Virasat-e-Khalsa is a large museum complex of Sikhism in Anandpur Sahib, Punjab, close to Takht Kesgarh Sahib.
facts.quote: Virasat-e-Khalsa, also known as the Khalsa Heritage Complex, is a mega-museum complex of Sikhism, located in the town of Anandpur Sahib, and is close to the Takht Kesgarh Sahib, located in the state of Punjab, India.

facts.fact: It opened on 25 November 2011, designed by Moshe Safdie to combine traditional Sikh elements with modernism.
facts.quote: The museum was inaugurated on the 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak on 25 November 2011. It architecture was designed by Moshe Safdie, incorporating both traditional Sikh architectural elements and modernism.

facts.fact: The buildings are cast-in-place concrete, partly exposed and largely clad in a local honey-coloured stone.
facts.quote: The buildings are constructed of poured-in-place concrete; some beams and columns remain exposed, though a great deal of the structures will be clad in a local honey-colored stone.

facts.fact: The roofs are clad in stainless steel and curve in two directions, while dams in the ravine make pools that reflect the complex.
facts.quote: The rooftops are stainless steel-clad and exhibit a double curvature: they gather and reflect the sky while a series of dams in the ravine create pools that reflect the entire complex at night.

facts.fact: The western complex holds an entrance plaza, a 400-seat auditorium, a two-storey library and changing galleries.
facts.quote: The smaller western complex includes an entrance plaza, an auditorium with 400 seating-capacity, two-story research and reference library, and changing exhibition galleries.

facts.fact: The turrets recall the old fortresses of Punjab, grouped in fives.
facts.quote: Safdie designed the turrets to resemble the old fortresses of Punjab, the cluster of five evoke the fortress architecture of the region (most evident in a nearby Gurdwara) and form a dramatic silhouette against the surrounding cliff terrain.

facts.fact: The galleries are grouped in fives to reflect the Five Virtues of Sikhism.
facts.quote: The gathering of the galleries in groups of five reflects the Five Virtues, a central tenet of Sikhism.

facts.fact: The complex covers more than a hundred acres.
facts.quote: The complex is located on over a hundred acres of land.

facts.fact: Raj Mandir is a cinema in Jaipur whose meringue-shaped auditorium opened in 1976.
facts.quote: Situated on the Bhagwan Das Road, near M.I. Road, the meringue-shaped auditorium opened in 1976, and over the years has seen many movie premieres of Hindi films, and has become a popular symbol of Jaipur.

facts.fact: It opened on 1 June 1976 with the film Charas.
facts.quote: Originally the brainchild of Mehtab Chandra Golcha, it opened on 1 June 1976 with the film "Charas" which was a charitable fund raiser show organized by Manav Hitkari Sangh.

facts.fact: W. M. Namjoshi designed it in the Art Moderne style, also called Streamline Moderne or late Art Deco.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect W. M. Namjoshi in Art Moderne style (Streamline Moderne or late Art Deco).

facts.fact: It was the 34th and last cinema designed by Namjoshi, who built cinemas across India from 1938 to 1976.
facts.quote: It was the last cinema built by the Jaipur-based Golcha/Surana family,  and also the  34th and last cinema hall designed by the architect, who designed cinema halls all over India, between 1938 and 1976, including art deco masterpieces like Golcha Cinema, Delhi (now closed), Kiran Cinema, Chandigarh and Maratha Mandir, Mumbai, .

facts.fact: The nine stars on the outside stand for the nine Navaratna gemstones, a nod to the owners' jewellery house.
facts.quote: The nine stars on the exterior signify nine gemstones in the Navaratna style, an homage to the owners' jewellery house.

facts.fact: It is described as the largest single-screen theatre in Asia.
facts.quote: An important landmark and tourist destination, the cinema hall has been accorded the status of largest single screen theatre in Asia.

facts.fact: Humayun's tomb in Delhi was commissioned by Empress Bega Begum and designed by the Persian architects Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and his son Sayyid Muhammad.
facts.quote: The tomb was commissioned by Humayun's first wife and chief consort, Empress Bega Begum, under her patronage in 1558, and designed by the Persian architects Mirak Mirza Ghiyas and his son, Sayyid Muhammad, whom she personally chose.

facts.fact: It was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent.
facts.quote: It was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, and is located in Nizamuddin East, Delhi, close to the Dina-panah Citadel, also known as Purana Qila (Old Fort), that Humayun founded in 1538.

facts.fact: Construction ran from 1565 to 1572.
facts.quote: Construction began in 1565 and was completed in 1572; it cost 1.5 million rupees, paid entirely by the Empress.

facts.fact: Built of rubble masonry and red sandstone, it uses white marble for cladding, floors, jaali screens, door frames, eaves and the main dome.
facts.quote: The tomb, built of rubble masonry and red sandstone, uses white marble as a cladding material and also for the flooring, lattice screens (jaalis), door frames, eaves (chhajja), and the main dome.

facts.fact: It was the first Indian building to use the Persian double dome on a high drum.
facts.quote: Inspired by Persian architecture; the tomb reaches a height of 47 metres (154 ft) and the plinth is 91 metres (299 ft) wide, and was the first Indian building to use the Persian double dome on a high neck drum, and measures 42.5 metres (139 ft), and is topped by 6 metres (20 ft) high brass finial ending in a crescent, common in Timurid tombs.

facts.fact: Inside, eight two-storey vaulted chambers radiate from a central double-height domed chamber in a ninefold square plan.
facts.quote: The symmetrical and simple design on the exterior is in sharp contrast with the complex interior floor plan, of the inner chambers, which is a square ninefold plan, where eight two-storied vaulted chambers radiate from the central, double-height domed chamber.

facts.fact: The tomb sits at the centre of a 30-acre charbagh, a Persian-style four-part garden, the first of its kind at this scale in South Asia.
facts.quote: While the main tomb took over eight years to build, it was also placed in the centre of a 30-acre (120,000 m2) charbagh, a Persian-style garden with a quadrilateral layout. It was the first of its kind in South Asia on such a scale.

facts.fact: It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
facts.quote: The tomb was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993, and has, thereafter, undergone extensive restoration work that has since concluded.

facts.fact: Modelled on Timur's tomb in Samarkand, it set the pattern for later Mughal royal tombs, culminating in the Taj Mahal.
facts.quote: Modelled after Gur-e Amir, the tomb of his ancestor and Asia's conqueror Timur in Samarkand, it established a precedent for future Mughal architecture of royal mausolea, which reached its zenith upon the construction of the Taj Mahal in Agra.

facts.fact: The ISKCON Temple Delhi is a Hindu temple to Krishna and Radha, opened on 5 April 1998 by Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
facts.quote: The temple was inaugurated on 5 April 1998 by the then Prime Minister of India, Atal Bihari Vajpayee in the presence of the former Chief Minister of Delhi, Sahib Singh Verma, and Sushma Swaraj.

facts.fact: It stands at Hare Krishna Hills, near Nehru Place, in Delhi's East of Kailash area.
facts.quote: It is located at Hare Krishna Hills (near Nehru Place), in East of Kailash area of Delhi, India.

facts.fact: Achyut Kanvinde designed it, taking the commission without fee in 1993; it is one of the largest temple complexes in India.
facts.quote: ISKCON Temple, designed and built by Achyut Kanvinde who in 1993 agreed to accept a pro-bono commission to build this temple complex for the followers of Srila Prabhupada, is one of the largest temple complexes in India.

facts.fact: The temple has a 375-seat auditorium for cultural and religious events.
facts.quote: The temple also has a 375-seater auditorium used for cultural and religious functions.

facts.fact: The church at Parumala, Kerala, is a pilgrimage centre and mausoleum of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.
facts.quote: St. Peter's and St. Paul's Orthodox Church (also known as Parumala Pally or  Parumala Seminary) in Parumala, Thiruvalla Taluk, Pathanamthitta district, Kerala, India, is a pilgrimage centre and mausoleum of the Malankara Orthodox Syrian Church.

facts.fact: It holds the tomb of Gregorios of Parumala, the first canonised Christian saint from India.
facts.quote: The church contains the tomb of the first canonized Christian saint from India, Gregorios of Parumala, who died on 2 November 1902 at the age of 54.

facts.fact: Designed by Charles Correa, the church seats more than 2,000 worshippers.
facts.quote: The church, which can accommodate more than 2000 worshipers, was designed by Charles Correa.

facts.fact: Its plan is a circle 39 m across inside, split into three segments by two 16 m chords.
facts.quote: It is a circle with an inner diameter of 39 meters, divided into three segments by two chords of 16 meters length.

facts.fact: The Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Telangana Secretariat in Hyderabad is the administrative office of the Government of Telangana.
facts.quote: Telangana Secretariat, officially known as Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Telangana Secretariat situated at Hyderabad, is the administrative office of the employees of the Government of Telangana in India.

facts.fact: It was designed by the Chennai architects Ponni Concessao and Oscar Concessao and built by Shapoorji Pallonji to Green Building Council norms.
facts.quote: Designed by Chennai-based Architects Ponni Concessao and Oscar Concessao, the complex has been built by Shapoorji Pallonji and Company Pvt Limited with all Green Building Council norms.

facts.fact: A 125-ft statue of Ambedkar stands beside it.
facts.quote: There is a 125-ft tall statue of Ambedkar beside the Telangana Secretariat.

facts.fact: Demolition of the old secretariat began in July 2020 to make way for the new complex.
facts.quote: The razing of old Secretariat complex of Telangana began in Hyderabad early in July 2020, with the government starting demolition of the old buildings and paving the way for construction of a state-of-the-art new complex in its place.

facts.fact: The new building is in the Indo-Saracenic style, with Indo-Islamic features such as domes.
facts.quote: Built in Indo-Saracenic style, the new Telangana Secretariat also blends the Indo-Islamic architectural features generally with domes.

facts.fact: Jehangir Art Gallery in Mumbai was founded by Sir Cowasji Jehangir and built in 1952.
facts.quote: It was founded by Sir Cowasji Jehangir at the urging of K. K. Hebbar and Homi J. Bhabha. It was built in 1952.

facts.fact: It stands at Kala Ghoda in South Mumbai and has four exhibition halls.
facts.quote: This gallery is situated at Kala Ghoda, behind the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya, in South Mumbai near the Gateway of India, and has four exhibition halls.

facts.fact: It opened on 21 January 1952, dedicated to the memory of Sir Cowasji's son, Jehangir.
facts.quote: The gallery was inaugurated on 21 January 1952, by then Chief Minister of Bombay State, B. G. Kher and dedicated it to the memory of Sir Cowasji's late son, Jehangir.

facts.fact: Designed by Durga Bajpai, it is one of the city's early concrete buildings.
facts.quote: The building has been designed by Durga Bajpai and is one of the early concrete structures in the city.

facts.fact: Because it combines an auditorium and galleries, the building turns inward, away from the street.
facts.quote: The gallery has been turned inwards due to a combined function of an auditorium and an art gallery.

facts.fact: A large wavy cantilevered entrance canopy reaches out to the street, and the plain facade has relief stone cladding.
facts.quote: The play with concrete can be easily seen with a large wavy cantilevered entrance which embraces the street. The otherwise bland facade is articulated with relief stone cladding.

facts.fact: The Nehru Centre in Mumbai promotes the ideals of Jawaharlal Nehru through educational and cultural programmes.
facts.quote: Nehru Centre is a centre to promote the teachings and ideals of the first Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, through educational and cultural programmes in the city of Mumbai, India.

facts.fact: It was conceived in 1972 and completed in 1985 on a six-acre site in Worli.
facts.quote: It was conceived in 1972, with foundation stone was laid by Indira Gandhi and the centre was completed in 1985 on a six-acre site in Worli.

facts.fact: Designed by I. M. Kadri, its cylindrical tower rising from a landscaped slope stands for India's growth from farming to industry.
facts.quote: Designed by architect I.M. Kadri, the building's distinctive cylindrical tower with an ascending landscaped slope at its base symbolizes Nehru's vision of India's growth from agrarian roots to industrial modernity.

facts.fact: The tower is clad in a latticed jaali inspired by the rose motif linked with Nehru.
facts.quote: The centerpiece is a cylindrical tower rising from a sloping green base evoking Nehru's metaphor of India growing from agriculture to industry and clad in latticed jaali inspired by the rose motif often associated with Nehru.

facts.fact: It covers about 322,000 sq ft, with a 1,000-seat auditorium, planetarium, art gallery, library and research facilities.
facts.quote: The centre spans approximately 322,000 sq ft, and includes a 1,000-seat auditorium, planetarium (commissioned in 1977), art gallery, library, and research facilities, organized within open-plan spaces and castellated beams to accommodate exhibitions and cultural events.

facts.fact: It was completed at a cost of ₹9 crore as a living memorial to India's first prime minister.
facts.quote: It was designed by I.M. Kadri, the centre was completed in 1985 at a cost of ₹9 crore, realized as a "living memorial" to India's first Prime Minister.

facts.fact: The Discovery of India exhibition has 14 galleries.
facts.quote: Discovery of India consists of 14 galleries depicting every aspect of artistic, intellectual and philosophical attainment of India through ages.

facts.fact: The Gateway of India is an arch-monument on Mumbai's waterfront, completed in 1924.
facts.quote: The Gateway of India is an arch-monument, completed in 1924, on the waterfront of Mumbai, Maharashtra, India.

facts.fact: It commemorates the landing of King George V in December 1911, the first visit of a British monarch to India.
facts.quote: It was erected to commemorate the landing of King George V of the United Kingdom for his coronation as the Emperor of India in December 1911 at Strand Road near Wellington Fountain. He was the first British monarch to visit India.

facts.fact: George Wittet's final design was approved in 1914, and the Indo-Saracenic monument draws on 16th-century Gujarati architecture.
facts.quote: The foundation stone was laid in March 1913 for a monument built in the Indo-Saracenic style, inspired by elements of 16th-century Gujarati architecture. The final design of the monument by architect George Wittet was sanctioned only in 1914, and construction was completed in 1924.

facts.fact: The arch is 26 m high, with a central dome 15 m across.
facts.quote: The Gateway's arch has a height of 26 metres (85 feet) with its central dome being 15 metres (49 feet) in diameter.

facts.fact: It is built of yellow basalt and reinforced concrete; the stone was local and the perforated screens came from Gwalior.
facts.quote: The monument is built of yellow basalt and reinforced concrete. The stones were sourced locally while the perforated screens were brought in from Gwalior.

facts.fact: Its facade recalls Gujarati mosque facades, while its basic form is an octopylon on eight piers, as in some triumphal arches.
facts.quote: The façade is reminiscent of Gujarati mosque façades, for example the Jama Mosque, Ahmedabad of 1424, while the basic shape is, in the terminology of classical architecture, an octopylon with a floor plan of eight piers, as used in some triumphal arches and memorials, including the Arc de Triomphe du Carrousel in Paris.

facts.fact: Large halls on each side of the arch can each hold 600 people.
facts.quote: On each side of the arch, there are large halls with the capacity to hold 600 people.

facts.fact: The approach road was never built for lack of funds, so the Gateway stands at an angle to the road leading to it.
facts.quote: Due to a paucity of funds, the approach road was never built. Hence, the Gateway stands at an angle to the road leading up to it.

facts.fact: The last British troops left India through the Gateway on 28 February 1948.
facts.quote: Following Indian independence, the last British troops to leave India, the First Battalion of the Somerset Light Infantry, passed through the Gateway with a 21-gun salute, as part of a ceremony on 28 February 1948, signalling the end of the British Raj.

facts.fact: Ravindra Bharathi is an auditorium in Hyderabad named after Rabindranath Tagore.
facts.quote: Ravindra Bharathi is an auditorium located in Hyderabad, Telangana, India. It was named after Rabindranath Tagore.

facts.fact: It was designed by Mohammad Fayazuddin, a graduate of the Architectural Association in London.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Mohammad Fayazuddin, an alumnus of Architectural Association School of Architecture, London.

facts.fact: It was built during the Tagore birth centenary and opened on 11 May 1961 by Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan.
facts.quote: Built during the birth centenary celebrations of Rabindranath Tagore, the auditorium was constructed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh for over a year. On 11 May 1961, former President of India, Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan inaugurated it to serve the cultural needs of the region.

facts.fact: In 2005 the interiors, lighting, acoustics, air-conditioning and stage were renovated.
facts.quote: As per that, the government spent ₹1.5 crore to improve the interiors, lighting, acoustics, air-conditioning, stage, green room.

facts.fact: The auditorium seats 1,104 and its stage is 105 ft wide, 48 ft deep and 38 ft high.
facts.quote: The auditorium has a plinth area of 2,295 square yards (1,919 m2) with a seating capacity of 1,104. The performing stage is 105 feet wide, 48 feet deep and 38 feet high.

facts.fact: The building has three floors: a main hall for about 1,000 people and two smaller halls of 150 and 112 seats.
facts.quote: The building consists of three floors—one main hall that can comfortably accommodate 1,000 people at once, and two others with a seating capacity of 150 and 112 people respectively.

facts.fact: The Mahindra United World College of India is an international boarding school about 40 km west of Pune.
facts.quote: The Mahindra United World College of India (MUWCI, also referred to as UWC Mahindra College or simply UWC Mahindra) is a pre-university international boarding school, located 40 km (25 mi) west of Pune in Maharashtra, India.

facts.fact: Nelson Mandela and Queen Noor of Jordan opened it on 28 November 1997.
facts.quote: On 28 November 1997, Queen Noor of Jordan and Nelson Mandela inaugurated the UWC Mahindra College in India.

facts.fact: Christopher Charles Benninger designed the campus, split into a residential and an academic area.
facts.quote: The campus was designed by architect Christopher Charles Benninger, and is divided into a residential and an academic area.

facts.fact: The design uses local materials and traditional Indian elements such as wadas, staggered steps and lotus ponds.
facts.quote: The design incorporates traditional elements and local building materials. Benninger paid homage to traditional Indian architecture by incorporating elements such as wadas, staggered steps, and lotus ponds.

facts.fact: The campus sits on a hill overlooking the Mula river valley near Mulshi Dam.
facts.quote: The MUWCI campus is situated on a hill surrounded by rural communities and overlooking the valley of the Mula river near Mulshi Dam.

facts.fact: Students live in houses of eight around shared courtyards, grouped into clusters called wadas.
facts.quote: The residential side of campus is divided into communal clusters called "Wadas". The Wadas house between 40 and 60 students and 4-6 teachers and families. Students live in independent houses of eight students each, with communal courtyards.

facts.fact: Business Week named it one of the ten super structures of the world in 2000.
facts.quote: Business Week called the Mahindra United World College of India one of the ten super structures of the world in 2000.

facts.fact: Benninger's work has been noted as one of the first instances of critical regionalism in India.
facts.quote: Benninger's work has been noted as one of the first instances of critical regionalism in India.

facts.fact: Ranga Shankara is a theatre in J.P. Nagar, south Bangalore, opened in 2004 in memory of the actor Shankar Nag.
facts.quote: It is located in the south Bangalore area of J.P Nagar and is run by the Sanket Trust. The auditorium, which opened in 2004, was envisioned by Arundathi Nag, in remembrance of her late husband, Shankar Nag, who was a renowned actor in the Kannada film industry.

facts.fact: The roughly ₹3 crore cost was raised through contributions, from ₹5 gifts to large sums from industrialists.
facts.quote: The entire cost of the project of around ₹3 crores. was raised through contributions, ranging from ₹5 from ordinary theatre lovers to big sums from industrialists.

facts.fact: Designed by Sharukh Mistry, it opened on 28 October 2004.
facts.quote: The Ranga shankara complex was designed by architect Sharukh Mistry and it was opened to the public on 28 October 2004.

facts.fact: Construction started only in 2001 for lack of funds.
facts.quote: However, due to lack of funds, construction only started in 2001.

facts.fact: The auditorium has a 1,575 sq ft thrust stage, with acoustics that need no amplification.
facts.quote: The auditorium has a thrust stage with a floor area of 1575 sq ft, with four green rooms and state-of-the-art sound, lighting, and technical facilities. The stage and the auditorium arrange the acoustics such that artificial amplification is not required.

facts.fact: The air-conditioned auditorium seats 320.
facts.quote: The auditorium is air conditioned and seats 320.

facts.fact: It keeps a 'play a day' policy, six days a week.
facts.quote: It follows an at least "a play a day" policy, six days a week (except on Mondays).

facts.fact: Nelum Pokuna is a performing arts centre in Colombo that opened on 15 December 2011.
facts.quote: is a performing arts centre in Colombo, Sri Lanka. The theatre opened on 15 December 2011.

facts.fact: Its architecture is inspired by the 12th-century Nelum Pokuna lotus pond at Polonnaruwa.
facts.quote: The architecture of the theatre is inspired by the 12th century Nelum Pokuna (lotus pond) in Polonnaruwa.

facts.fact: The building has about 14,000 m2 of floor area.
facts.quote: The building spreads over 14,000 m2 (150,000 sq ft) of floor area.

facts.fact: It holds a 1,288-seat auditorium, a library and training facilities.
facts.quote: The theatre is equipped with an auditorium with 1,288 seats, a library, and training facilities.

facts.fact: Besides the main auditorium there is an open-air theatre, and the front steps can become a second one.
facts.quote: The building features two permanent theatres—the main auditorium and an open-air theatre—and the ability to convert the front steps into an additional open-air theatre.

facts.fact: The auditorium has a 690 m2 moving stage, with an orchestra pit that rises to stage level.
facts.quote: The 690 m2 (7,400 sq ft) moving stage in the auditorium includes the ability to raise and lower the orchestra pit to and from stage level.

facts.fact: The Chinese government provided most of the funding.
facts.quote: The total estimated cost of the project is LKR 3,080 million. Government of the People's Republic of China provided LKR 2430 million out of the total cost of the building.

facts.fact: Designed by Kahawita De Silva & Associates, it borrows a historic landscape feature to make a modern national monument to the arts.
facts.quote: The Nelum Pokuna Mahinda Rajapaksa Theatre in Colombo, by Kahawita De Silva & Associates, is an example of using a historical landscape design feature, the Nelum Pokuna in Polonnaruwa, to create a modern national monument to celebrate the country's arts.

facts.fact: The memorial at Rayerbazar, Dhaka, honours the intellectuals killed in the Bangladesh Liberation War.
facts.quote: Martyred Intellectuals Memorial (Bengali: শহীদ বুদ্ধিজীবী স্মৃতিসৌধ) is a monument built in memory of the martyred intellectuals of the Bangladesh Liberation War. The memorial is located at Rayerbazar, Mohammadpur Thana in Dhaka.

facts.fact: Farid Uddin Ahmed and Md Jami-al-Shafi won a national competition of 22 entries for its design.
facts.quote: Out of 22 entries, the jurors selected the design proposal of architect Farid Uddin Ahmed and architect Md Jami-al-Shafi.

facts.fact: It was built from 1996 to 1999.
facts.quote: Its completion took about three years (1996 to 1999).

facts.fact: Its main element is a curved brick wall about 17.7 m high, 0.9 m thick and 115.8 m long, recalling the Rayer Bazar brickfield where the bodies were found.
facts.quote: The main element of the monument is approximately 17.7 m high, 0.9 m thick and 115.8 m long curved brick wall, representing the original brickfield of Rayer Bazar where the dead bodies were found.

facts.fact: The wall is broken at both ends to represent grief and sorrow.
facts.quote: The wall is broken at the two ends, representing grief and sorrow.

facts.fact: A square window in the wall frames the sky behind and scales the wall down.
facts.quote: A square window at the south-west side of the wall permits visitor's view to reach the sky behind, that also scale down the wall.

facts.fact: In front of the wall a black granite column rises from still water, representing grief.
facts.quote: In front of the curved wall is a still water body from which rises a black granite column, which represents grief.

facts.fact: The mausoleum in Dhaka holds the graves of A. K. Fazlul Huq, Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy and Khwaja Nazimuddin.
facts.quote: It contains the graves of three prominent leaders of Pakistan Movement from Bengal:  A. K. Fazlul Huq, Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy and Khwaja Nazimuddin.

facts.fact: It stands in Suhrawardy Udyan, Shahbagh, near the University of Dhaka.
facts.quote: It is located in Suhrawardy Udyan in Shahbagh across from the Doel Square near the University of Dhaka.

facts.fact: It was completed in 1986.
facts.quote: Eventually, the construction of the mausoleum was completed in 1986 during the presidency of Hussain Muhammad Ershad.

facts.fact: It was designed by Masud Ahmad and S. A. Zahiruddin as an interpretation of Islamic arches.
facts.quote: It was designed by architect Masud Ahmad and S. A. Zahiruddin. The style of architecture of the monuments is an interpretation of Islamic Arcs.

facts.fact: A hyperbolic paraboloid structure is raised over the three graves.
facts.quote: The Mausoleum of three leaders consists of a hyperbolic paraboloid structure that is erected over the three graves of the three political leaders.

facts.fact: The real tombs lie underground, with replicas of the graves below the monument.
facts.quote: Although you have to go underground to see the three tombs located here, there are replicas of three graves below the monument.

facts.fact: The Sixty Dome Mosque in Bagerhat is part of the Mosque City of Bagerhat, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
facts.quote: The Sixty Dome Mosque (Bengali: ষাট গম্বুজ মসজিদ) is a historical mosque, located in Bagerhat, in the Khulna Division of Bangladesh. It is a part of the Mosque City of Bagerhat, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: It is the largest mosque in Bangladesh from the Bengal Sultanate period, built by Khan Jahan Ali.
facts.quote: It is the largest mosque in Bangladesh from the Bengal Sultanate period (1352–1576). It was built by Khan Jahan Ali, the governor of the Sundarbans.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1442 and finished in 1459; it served as mosque, madrasa and assembly hall.
facts.quote: The construction of the mosque began in 1442 and was completed in 1459. The mosque was used for prayers as well as served as a madrasha and assembly hall.

facts.fact: Despite its name, it has 81 domes carried on sixty columns.
facts.quote: Despite its nomenclature, the mosque has 81 domes that are supported by sixty columns.

facts.fact: It has very thick, tapered brick walls in the Tughlaq style and a hut-shaped roofline.
facts.quote: The Sixty Dome Mosque features unusually thick, tapered brick walls in the Tughlaq style and a hut-shaped roofline that anticipates later styles.

facts.fact: The oblong plan measures about 45 by 31 m outside.
facts.quote: Its oblong plan measures 45.26 metres (148 ft 6 in) by 30.89 metres (101 ft 4 in) externally, and 37.57 metres (123 ft 3 in) by 23.22 metres (76 ft 2 in) internally.

facts.fact: Seventy-seven low domes sit in seven rows of eleven, with one more on each corner.
facts.quote: There are 77 low domes arranged in seven rows of eleven, with an additional dome on each corner, bringing the total to 81 domes.

facts.fact: The western wall has eleven mihrabs inside, ten of them blind.
facts.quote: The western wall features eleven mihrabs on the interior where ten are blind and the central one is projected on the exterior.

facts.fact: Hatirjheel is a lakefront in Dhaka, with roads and bridges built around it to ease traffic.
facts.quote: Hatirjheel (Bengali: হাতিরঝিল [ɦatir dʒʱil], English: ; lit. Lake of Elephant) is a lakefront in Dhaka, Bangladesh with surrounding roads and bridges built to ease traffic congestion.

facts.fact: Development began in 2008 with roads, bridges and a water retention area, and the site opened to the public in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2008, the government launched a development project that included the construction of roads, bridges, and a water retention area. The site was officially opened to the public in 2013 and is now a popular recreational spot for residents of Dhaka.

facts.fact: The project was led by architect Iqbal Habib with Ehsan Khan and Ishtiaque Zahir of VITTI Sthapati Brindo.
facts.quote: The project was led by architect Iqbal Habib (Team Leader), Ehsan Khan and Ishtiaque Zahir of VITTI Sthapati Brindo Ltd.

facts.fact: The project covers 302 acres.
facts.quote: The project, covering 302 acres (1.22 km2), was later revised to a cost of ৳2236.02 crore (US$180 million).

facts.fact: It was meant to tackle traffic and also keep one of the city's key water retention basins and drainage channels.
facts.quote: The concept for developing Hatirjheel first emerged in 1995, aiming to address Dhaka’s traffic congestion and improve public mobility, while also preserving one of the city's key natural water retention basins and drainage channels linking old and new Dhaka.

facts.fact: The works include an 8.8 km expressway, service roads, four bridges, four overpasses, three viaducts and two U-loops.
facts.quote: As part of the development project, an 8.8-kilometre (5.5 mi) expressway, 9.8 kilometres (6.1 mi) of service roads, four bridges, four overpasses, three viaducts, and two U-loops were constructed to improve connectivity and traffic flow across the area.

facts.fact: There is an amphitheatre for 2,000 visitors.
facts.quote: The area has an amphitheatre with a capacity to accommodate 2,000 visitors.

facts.fact: Poor sewage infrastructure has left the lake heavily polluted, so it has not worked as intended as a rainwater store.
facts.quote: Despite being developed as a rainwater retention facility, Hatirjheel has failed to fulfil its intended purpose, primarily due to inadequate sewage infrastructure that has led to severe pollution from sewage runoff.

facts.fact: In Pakistan, the Turkish architect Vedat Dalokay designed the Summit Minar monument in Lahore, and is seen as a major Turkish influence on Pakistani architecture.
facts.quote: In Pakistan, he was also the architect of two not realized buildings, then of the constricted monument Summit Minar, Lahore and is considered a major Turkish influence in Pakistani architecture.

facts.fact: Dalokay is best known as the designer of the Faisal Mosque in Islamabad.
facts.quote: He is best known for being the designer of the Faisal Mosque in Islamabad.

facts.fact: Expo Centre Lahore is a convention centre designed by a joint venture of NESPAK and Nayyar Ali Dada & Associates.
facts.quote: Designed by joint venture of National Engineering Services Pakistan (NESPAK) and Nayyar Ali Dada & Associates, the convention center is located in Johar Town at the corner of Abdul Haque Road and Shahrah Nazaria-e-Pakistan.

facts.fact: Construction ran from 2007 to 2010.
facts.quote: Construction began in 2007 and was completed in 2010.

facts.fact: It was built jointly by the provincial and federal governments on a 400-kanal plot leased from the Lahore Development Authority.
facts.quote: The centre was established jointly by the provincial and federal governments of Pakistan at a 400-kanal land plot provided by the Lahore Development Authority on a 40-years lease in 2004.

facts.fact: It was meant to give exporters one central place to show their products to foreign buyers.
facts.quote: The intent was to provide local exporters a central location for displaying their products and providing product information to foreign trade delegations and buyers under one roof.

facts.fact: In 2020 it held a temporary COVID-19 field hospital.
facts.quote: In 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic crisis, a temporary field hospital was set up at the Expo Centre to deal with the emergency overflow of patients that could not be accommodated at the many hospitals in and around the city of Lahore.

facts.fact: The KCCI Building is a heritage building of 1934 in central Karachi, now the headquarters of the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry.
facts.quote: The Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry Building, also known as the KCCI Building, is a heritage building in central Karachi, Pakistan dating from 1934. Its foundation stone was laid by Gandhi in July 1934. It currently serves as headquarters for the Karachi Chamber of Commerce & Industry.

facts.fact: Gandhi laid its foundation stone on 8 July 1934, for the Karachi Indian Merchants' Association.
facts.quote: Mahatma Gandhi laid the foundation stone for the building on July 8, 1934, to serve as the headquarters of the Karachi Indian Merchants' Association.

facts.fact: It was declared a protected heritage site on 7 September 1995.
facts.quote: It was declared a protected heritage site on 7 September 1995.

facts.fact: The exterior is largely unchanged, but the interior has been heavily altered.
facts.quote: Although the exterior remains largely unchanged from its original design, the interior has been heavily modified over time.

facts.fact: Ahmed Hussain Agha designed it in the Anglo-Mughal revival style popular in the 1920s.
facts.quote: Ahmed Hussain Agha designed the structure in the Mughal-revival style known as Anglo-Mughal, which was popular in the 1920s.

facts.fact: Unlike earlier European-style civic buildings in Karachi, it draws heavily on Mughal architecture.
facts.quote: The KCCI Building differs from earlier civic structures in the city in that it is heavily influenced by Mughal architecture.

facts.fact: It is built of sandstone, with some materials brought from Jaipur.
facts.quote: It was constructed of sandstone, with some materials brought from Jaipur, now in the Indian state of Rajasthan.

facts.fact: Mohatta Palace, also called Qasr-e-Fatima, is a museum in Karachi designed by Ahmed Hussain Agha and built in 1927 as the summer home of Shivratan Mohatta.
facts.quote: Designed by Ahmed Hussain Agha, the palace was built in 1927 in the affluent seaside suburb of Clifton as the summer home of Shivratan Mohatta, a Hindu Marwari businessman from what is now the modern-day Indian state of Rajasthan.

facts.fact: Following the stone palaces of Rajasthan, it uses pink Jodhpur stone with local yellow stone from Gizri.
facts.quote: The palace was built in the tradition of stone palaces of Rajasthan, using pink Jodhpur stone in combination with the local yellow stone from nearby Gizri.

facts.fact: The palace covers 1,720 m2 and has nine domes, with one at the centre.
facts.quote: The palace has an area of 1,720 m2 (18,500 sq ft) and its façade is trimmed with windows, stone brackets, spandrels, domes, balustrades with floral motifs and exquisite railings. There are nine domes, with a centre dome in the middle; while the windows in the front portion opening out into the garden are of blue colour and those in the rear area are arched windows with stained glass.

facts.fact: Grand rooms for entertaining are on the ground floor, with private rooms and a shaded terrace above.
facts.quote: The palace has large stately rooms designed for entertainment on the ground floor and more private facilities on the first floor, where there is a terrace provided with a shade from intense sunlight.

facts.fact: Octagonal towers stand at each corner of the palace.
facts.quote: On each corner of the palace are octagonal towers, in which only two near the front entrance have spiral staircases that go up to the roof.

facts.fact: Peacock motifs are carved in the stonework around each of the nine domes.
facts.quote: There are also peacock motifs in the stonework and they are found around each of the nine domes.

facts.fact: The Government of Sindh bought it in 1995 to become a museum of the arts of Pakistan.
facts.quote: In 1995 it was purchased by the Government of Sindh for its conversion into a museum devoted to the arts of Pakistan.

facts.fact: Mohatta Palace Museum opened in 1999.
facts.quote: Mohatta Palace Museum formally opened in 1999.

facts.fact: Frere Hall in Karachi was completed in 1865 as the town hall and is now an exhibition space and library.
facts.quote: Completed in 1865, Frere Hall was originally intended to serve as Karachi's town hall, and now serves as an exhibition space and library.

facts.fact: Henry Saint Clair Wilkins was chosen from 12 candidates to design it.
facts.quote: The building was intended to serve as Karachi's town hall, and was designed by Henry Saint Clair Wilkins, who was chosen from among 12 candidates.

facts.fact: Work ran from August 1863 to October 1865.
facts.quote: Work commenced in August 1863 and continued until October 1865; construction had not been entirely completed by the time of its inauguration.

facts.fact: It is Venetian-Gothic with British and local elements: pointed arches, ribbed vaults, quatrefoils and flying buttresses.
facts.quote: Frere Hall was built in the Venetian-Gothic style that also blends elements of British and local architecture. The building features multiple pointed arches, ribbed vaults, quatrefoils, and flying buttresses.

facts.fact: It is built mainly of local yellow limestone, with white oolite details from Bholari.
facts.quote: The building is built primarily out of local yellow-toned limestone, with stone details formed from white oolite stone quarried from the nearby town of Bholari.

facts.fact: A tall octagonal corner tower is crowned by an iron cage, and the roof is coated with Muntz metal.
facts.quote: A tall octagonal tower is located in one of the building's corner that is crowned by an iron cage. The roof of the hall is coated with Muntz metal.

facts.fact: Sadequain painted its ceilings in the 1980s; one mural was left unfinished at his death in 1987.
facts.quote: The hall's ceilings were decorated by the world-renowned Pakistani artist Sadequain in the 1980s, with one mural remaining incomplete after his death in 1987.

facts.fact: The Lahore Museum is among the works of Bhai Ram Singh, one of pre-partition Punjab's foremost architects.
facts.quote: Bhai Ram Singh  (1858–1916) was one of pre-partition Punjab's foremost architects, dominating the scene for nearly two decades from the 1890s. Amongst his works is the Durbar Room, Osborne House, on the Isle of Wight, England; Lahore Museum and Governor's House in Simla.

facts.fact: Most of Bhai Ram Singh's work is Indo-Saracenic, a style in which he was the most significant Indian architect.
facts.quote: Most of his work fits under the style of Indo-Saracenic architecture, of which he was the most significant Indian architect.

facts.fact: Nyayo House is a government skyscraper in Nairobi housing departments such as immigration.
facts.quote: Nyayo House is a skyscraper in Nairobi, Kenya. It hosts several government departments such as immigration (the State Department for Immigration, Border Control, and Regulation of Persons) and also serves as the headquarters of Nairobi Province.

facts.fact: It stands at the corner of Uhuru Highway and Kenyatta Avenue, 84 m high with 27 floors.
facts.quote: The building is located at the corner of Uhuru Highway and Kenyatta Avenue. It is 84 metres high and has 27 floors.

facts.fact: Planning began in 1973, when it was to be called Nairobi House.
facts.quote: Planning of the tower started in 1973 and it was initially set to be named Nairobi House.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1979 and finished in 1983.
facts.quote: Construction started in 1979, one year after Daniel arap Moi took over as the president of Kenya. Building of the house was completed in 1983.

facts.fact: It was planned by the Ministry of Public Works and Ngotho Architects, and built by Laxmanbhai Construction.
facts.quote: The building was planned by Ministry of Public Works, Ngotho Architects and constructed by Laxmanbhai Construction.

facts.fact: Its basement held detention cells, known as the Nyayo House torture chambers, where opponents of the Moi government were beaten.
facts.quote: Nyayo House is particularly known for its detention facilities in its basement, often called "Nyayo House torture chambers". Many opponents of the Moi government were beaten there by Special Branch officials (the Special Branch was later renamed the National Security Intelligence Service).

facts.fact: The Tintenpalast in Windhoek is the seat of both houses of Namibia's Parliament.
facts.quote: The Parliament Building, Windhoek, also known as the Tintenpalast (German for Ink Palace), is the seat of both houses of the Parliament of Namibia (the National Council and the National Assembly).
