facts.fact: Gottlieb Redecker designed it with a Neoclassical front, and Sander & Kock built it from regional materials in 1912-1913 as a German colonial administration building.
facts.quote: The Tintenpalast, which is located just north of Robert Mugabe Avenue, was designed by German architect Gottlieb Redecker with a Neoclassical front façade and built by the company Sander & Kock between 1912 and 1913 from regional materials as an administration building for the German government, which colonised Namibia at the time.

facts.fact: It was built with forced labour by Herero and Nama survivors of the genocide held in concentration camps.
facts.quote: The building project used forced labour by Herero and Nama people who, having survived the Herero and Nama genocide, had been placed in concentration camps.

facts.fact: It opened on 12 April 1913 and was nicknamed 'Ink Palace' for the ink used by the officials who worked there.
facts.quote: The building was opened on 12 April 1913. As an allusion to the extensive usage of ink by the workers in the building, it was named "Tintenpalast" or "Ink Palace".

facts.fact: At independence in 1990 it became the seat of the National Assembly.
facts.quote: When Namibia achieved its independence in 1990, the Tintenpalast became the seat of the National Assembly.

facts.fact: It is surrounded by the Parliament Gardens, popular with Windhoek's residents.
facts.quote: The Tintenpalast is surrounded by the Parliament Gardens, which is very popular among the inhabitants of Windhoek.

facts.fact: Maputo City Hall is the seat of the city's government, a Neoclassical building at the head of Independence Square, erected in 1947.
facts.quote: The neoclassical building is located at the head of Praça da Independência (Independence Square), and was erected in 1947.

facts.fact: The Portuguese-Brazilian architect Carlos César dos Santos won the design competition in 1938.
facts.quote: The Portuguese-Brazilian architect Carlos César dos Santos won the competition in 1938.

facts.fact: Construction began in 1941 and finished in 1947.
facts.quote: In 1941, the new mayor, Francisco dos Santos Pinto Teixeira, started construction works on the new building, which was built facing on to Praça Mouzinho de Albuquerque (renamed Praça da Independência in 1975). It was finished in 1947.

facts.fact: Set on a hill on a trapezoidal plan, it closes the view along today's Samora Machel Avenue from the downtown.
facts.quote: Santos designed the new Câmara Municipal Building (the new City Hall) with a trapezoidal layout situated on a hill, so it became automatically the focal point of the Avenida D. Luis (today Samora Machel Avenue), which connects the Independence Square with the city's downtown area, (Baixa).

facts.fact: Its facade is 65 m long, fully Neoclassical and following Beaux-Arts rules.
facts.quote: The city hall has a façade of 65 metres (213 ft) and is completely designed in the Neoclassical fashion and follows the architectonic beaux-art rules.

facts.fact: To save money, artificial stone was used instead of cut stone.
facts.quote: Owing to financial constraints, the city government chose artificial stone instead of dimension stone.

facts.fact: It was added to Maputo's list of cultural monuments in 2011.
facts.quote: The Maputo City Hall was added to the list of cultural monuments of Maputo in 2011.

facts.fact: Maputo Cathedral is a Catholic cathedral on Independence Square, next to the City Hall.
facts.quote: The cathedral is located on Praça da Independência (Independence Square) next to Hotel Rovuma and Maputo City Hall.

facts.fact: The foundation stone was laid on 28 June 1936 and the cathedral was finished in 1944.
facts.quote: The foundation stone for the construction of the church was laid on June 28, 1936, and is located inside the narthex and inscribed by the Bishop of Mozambique and Cape Verde, D. Rafael Maria da Asunção. Construction on the cathedral was completed in 1944.

facts.fact: It was designed by the Portuguese civil engineer Marcial Simões de Freitas e Costa, then a railway director.
facts.quote: The cathedral was designed by the Portuguese civil engineer Marcial Simões de Freitas e Costa, then a railway director.

facts.fact: He designed it without fee for the Archdiocese.
facts.quote: He designed the church pro bono for the Archdiocese of Lourenço Marques.

facts.fact: Following the simple European churches of the time, it was built of concrete and cement.
facts.quote: Freitas was inspired by the simple style and building materials of church construction in Europe of the time; the cathedral was ultimately built of concrete and cement.

facts.fact: Its models included Auguste Perret's Notre-Dame du Raincy and Pardal Monteiro's Our Lady of Fátima in Lisbon.
facts.quote: He was inspired to buildings such as the Notre-Dame du Raincy in Le Raincy (1921-1923) by Auguste Perret and Igreja de Nossa Senhora de Fátima (1934-1938) in Lisbon, built by Pardal Monteiro.

facts.fact: St. George's Cathedral is an Ethiopian Orthodox church in Addis Ababa known for its octagonal form.
facts.quote: Saint George's Cathedral (Amharic: የቅዱስ ጊዮርጊስ ካቴድራል) is an Ethiopian Orthodox church in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The cathedral is noted for its distinctive octagonal form.

facts.fact: It stands on the ruins of a 15th-century church.
facts.quote: The new church was built on the ruins of an older church from the 15th century.

facts.fact: The Italian engineer Sebastiano Castagna designed and built it in 1911.
facts.quote: The building was designed and built by the Italian engineer Sebastiano Castagna in 1911.

facts.fact: Empress Zewditu was crowned here in 1917 and Emperor Haile Selassie in 1930.
facts.quote: Empress Zewditu was crowned at this Cathedral in 1917, and Emperor Haile Selassie was crowned there in 1930, and it became a pilgrimage site for Rastafarians.

facts.fact: A 1938 Italian guide called it a fine example of a European reading of Ethiopian church design.
facts.quote: The building was described in 1938 in an Italian tourist publication as a fine example of the European interpretation of Ethiopian church design.

facts.fact: Set on fire by the Italian Fascist authorities in 1937, it was restored by Haile Selassie after 1941.
facts.quote: The Italian Fascist authorities set the building on fire in 1937. The cathedral was later restored by Emperor Haile Selassie following the liberation in 1941.

facts.fact: Munyonyo Martyrs' Shrine is a Catholic shrine and Minor Basilica dedicated to the Ugandan Martyrs.
facts.quote: The Munyonyo Martyrs’ Shrine is a Roman Catholic shrine and Minor Basilica dedicated to the Ugandan Martyrs.

facts.fact: It stands at Munyonyo, about 13 km south of central Kampala.
facts.quote: Munyonyo is located approximately 13 kilometres (8.1 mi), by road, south of the central business district of Kampala, Uganda's capital and largest city.

facts.fact: It marks the place where King Mwanga decided to begin putting Christians to death in 1886.
facts.quote: It was at Munyonyo where King Mwanga took the fateful decision to begin putting Christians to death.

facts.fact: Ground was broken on 3 May 2015 for a new church, museum, offices and martyrdom spots.
facts.quote: Official groundbreaking was on 3 May 2015 by Papal Nuncio to Uganda; Archbishop Michael A. Blume and Cardinal Emmanuel Wamala. Redevelopment includes construction of new church shrine, museum, offices and martyrdom spots of the saints.

facts.fact: Pope Francis blessed the cornerstone on 27 November 2015.
facts.quote: Pope Francis visited and blessed the cornerstone of the Shrine on 27 November 2015 during his journey to Africa.

facts.fact: The new church was finished in 2016 and consecrated on 28 October 2017.
facts.quote: The construction of the new church was completed in 2016 and the shrine was consecrated on 28 October 2017 by Cardinal Fernando Filoni.

facts.fact: The Holy See made it a Minor Basilica on 19 July 2019.
facts.quote: On 19 July 2019, The Holy See granted the church the title and dignity of a Minor Basilica.

facts.fact: The Hôtel du Lac in Tunis was designed in the Brutalist style by Italian architect Raffaele Contigiani and built from 1970 to 1973 for Habib Bourguiba's government.
facts.quote: The building was designed in the Brutalist style by the Italian architect Raffaele Contigiani and built from 1970 to 1973 for the Tunisian government of Habib Bourguiba.

facts.fact: It stands at the eastern end of Avenue Habib Bourguiba, west of the Lake of Tunis.
facts.quote: The hotel stands to the north of the Place du 14 – Janvier 2011 (formerly the Place du 7 – Novembre 1987) at the eastern end of Avenue Habib Bourguiba, between Avenue Mohammed V and A1 motorway, to the west of the Lake of Tunis.

facts.fact: It rests on 190 reinforced-concrete piles up to 60 m deep and is a single ten-storey block of béton brut around a steel frame.
facts.quote: It was constructed on 190 reinforced concrete piles up to 60 m (200 ft) deep, and built from exposed concrete (béton brut) around a steel structure, creating a single long block with ten floors, with large windows.

facts.fact: Cantilevered stairs projecting at each end give it an inverted-pyramid shape.
facts.quote: Projecting cantilevered stairs at each end create an inverted pyramid shape.

facts.fact: Most of its 416 bedrooms are on the upper floors, and the top floor is twice as long as the ground floor.
facts.quote: The 416 bedrooms are mostly on the upper floors, with the top floor twice as long as the ground floor.

facts.fact: Breaking with Arab and European tradition, it became a symbol of modernism in Tunis and is an important example of Brutalism in North Africa.
facts.quote: The striking design, departing from traditional Arab and European architecture, made the hotel a symbol of modernism in Tunis.  It remains an important example of Brutalism in North Africa.

facts.fact: Its shape has been compared to the sandcrawler in the Star Wars films.
facts.quote: Its distinctive shape has prompted comparisons with the sandcrawler vehicle of the Star Wars films.

facts.fact: It closed in 2000 after falling into disrepair, and its demolition has been threatened.
facts.quote: The hotel was privatised in the 1990s, but fell into disrepair and closed in 2000.

facts.fact: The mausoleum at Aswan holds Aga Khan III and, since 2025, Aga Khan IV.
facts.quote: The mausoleum is located at Aswan along the Nile of Egypt, since Egypt was formerly the centre of power of the Fatimids, an Ismaili Shia dynasty. It is now also the resting place of Aga Khan IV (Karim al-Hussaini, who died in 2025).

facts.fact: It was built from 1956 to 1960, commissioned by Begum Om Habibeh Aga Khan.
facts.quote: The construction of the mausoleum began in 1956 and ended in 1960. The Aga Khan III's wife, Begum Om Habibeh Aga Khan, commissioned the construction of the mausoleum, which initially accepted tourists inside; however, the interior was closed off to the public in 1997.

facts.fact: It sits on a hill on the west bank of the Nile, above a villa designed by Hassan Fathy.
facts.quote: The mausoleum sits atop a hill along the west bank of the Nile, where it overlooks the villa of Aga Khan III and Begum Om Habibeh, later the home of Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan. The villa was designed by Egyptian architect Hassan Fathy, and it served as a winter home for Aga Khan III, whose will stated that he would be buried near the villa two years after his death.

facts.fact: It was designed to resemble the Fatimid Juyushi Mosque of 1085, with a rectangular plan, high walls, a central dome and smaller domes.
facts.quote: The Mausoleum of Aga Khan III was designed to resemble the Masjid al-Juyushi, a Fatimid mosque and dedicated mausoleum that was constructed in 1085. Both the Masjid al-Juyushi and the Mausoleum of Aga Khan III feature a rectangular layout with high walls, a central dome, and numerous smaller domes.

facts.fact: Its architect, Farid Shafi'e, had studied Fatimid architecture extensively.
facts.quote: Shafi'e's past publications indicate that he had studied Fatimid architecture extensively prior to designing the Mausoleum of Aga Khan III.

facts.fact: It is built of pink limestone with crenellated parapets and a single arched entrance on the west.
facts.quote: The Mausoleum of Aga Khan III is built of pink limestone. Crenellated parapets line the outer wall, and an arched doorway on the western side of mausoleum serves as the only entrance to the mausoleum's interior.

facts.fact: A large central dome with arched tracery windows rises on an octagonal drum, with small domes at the four corners.
facts.quote: The eastern side of the mausoleum features a large central dome with arched tracery windows along the octagonal drum. Four miniature domes are located on each corner of the outer wall.

facts.fact: The tomb inside is Carrara marble with Quranic inscriptions.
facts.quote: Quran'ic inscriptions adorn the interior tomb of Aga Khan III, which is made of Carrara marble.

facts.fact: FNB Stadium, also called Soccer City or the Calabash, is a football and rugby stadium at Nasrec, bordering Soweto in Johannesburg.
facts.quote: The First National Bank (FNB) Stadium, also known as Soccer City or the Calabash, is a football and rugby union stadium located in Nasrec, bordering the Soweto area of Johannesburg, South Africa.

facts.fact: Built as the main stadium of the 2010 World Cup, it became the largest stadium in Africa, holding 94,736.
facts.quote: Designed as the main association football stadium for the 2010 World Cup, the FNB Stadium became the largest stadium in Africa with a capacity of 94,736.

facts.fact: The original stadium of 1987 was redesigned for 2010 by HOK Sport (now Populous) and Boogertman + Partners, inspired by the calabash, an African pot.
facts.quote: Built in 1987, the stadium underwent a major upgrade for the 2010 FIFA World Cup, with a new design inspired by the shape of an African pot, the calabash. The South African main contractor GLTA, part of the Aveng Group in a joint venture with the Dutch company BAM who had a 25% stake, constructed the upgrade, which was designed by HOK Sport (now known as Populous) and Boogertman + Partners.

facts.fact: The upgrade added an extended upper tier, an encircling roof, new changing rooms and floodlights.
facts.quote: The upgrade included: an extended upper tier around the stadium to increase the capacity to 88,958, an additional two executive suites, an encircling roof, new changing room facilities and new floodlights.

facts.fact: The outer cladding is a mosaic of fire and earth colours, with a ring of lights at the base like fire under the pot.
facts.quote: The outside of the stadium is designed to have the appearance of an African pot; the cladding on the outside is a mosaic of fire and earthen colours with a ring of lights running around the bottom of the structure, simulating fire underneath the pot.

facts.fact: No spectator sits more than 100 m from the field, and no view is blocked.
facts.quote: No spectator is seated more than 100 metres (330 ft) from the field, and there are no restricted views in the stadium.

facts.fact: Ten black lines in the stands point to the nine other 2010 World Cup stadiums and to Berlin's Olympic Stadium.
facts.quote: The stands in the FNB Stadium are articulated by ten black vertical lines; nine are aligned geographically with the nine other stadiums involved in the 2010 World Cup.

facts.fact: It hosted the 2010 World Cup Final, and Nelson Mandela's first Johannesburg speech after his release in 1990.
facts.quote: It was the site of Nelson Mandela's first speech in Johannesburg after his release from prison in 1990, and served as the venue for a memorial service to him on 10 December 2013.

facts.fact: Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium in Gqeberha is a football and rugby stadium that hosted 2010 World Cup matches.
facts.quote: The Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium is a soccer and rugby union stadium in Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. It hosted 2010 FIFA World Cup matches, including the third-place play off.

facts.fact: It overlooks the lake at the heart of the city, one of three coastal stadiums built for the 2010 World Cup.
facts.quote: The five-tier, R2 billion (approximately US$159 million) Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium was built overlooking the South End Lake, at the heart of the city, one of three coastal stadiums built to host the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

facts.fact: Its roof is a series of white 'petals' like a flower, which gave it the nickname The Protea.
facts.quote: The roof is made up of a series of white 'petals' making it look like a flower. This is the reason for the stadium's nickname, The Protea.

facts.fact: The building is about 40 m high, and the main architects were Architectural Design Associates and Dominic Bonnesse Architects.
facts.quote: The stadium building is approximately 40m high and consists of six levels on the western side in addition to five on each of the north, south and east stands. The main architecture was handled by Architectural Design Associates(Pty)Ltd and Dominic Bonnesse Architects cc.

facts.fact: It seats 46,000, plus 4,000 temporary seats for the 2010 World Cup.
facts.quote: The stadium seats 46,000 in addition to 4,000 extra seats temporarily installed for the 2010 FIFA World Cup.

facts.fact: Seats in shades from light orange to dark red are mixed seemingly at random so the stadium always looks full.
facts.quote: The seats are of different shades, from light orange to dark red. They are arranged seemingly at random, but this was done to help the stadium appear full at all times.

facts.fact: The roof combines aluminium cladding with PTFE-coated glass-fibre membrane on a steel superstructure.
facts.quote: The roof material of the stadium consists of a combination of aluminium cladding, combined with a membrane material called polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), which is a coated glass-fibre fabric and steel superstructure.

facts.fact: It was the first of five new 2010 World Cup stadiums to start construction.
facts.quote: The Nelson Mandela Bay Stadium was the first of five new stadiums to start construction.

facts.fact: Pretoria railway station is the city's central station, in a 1910 building by Herbert Baker.
facts.quote: It is located between Pretoria's central business district and Salvokop, in a 1910 building designed by Herbert Baker.

facts.fact: Pretoria's first station was built in 1892 by the Netherlands-South African Railway Company.
facts.quote: The first railway station in Pretoria was built in 1892 by the Netherlands-South African Railway Company (NZASM) as the western terminus of its line to the harbour of Delagoa Bay (now Maputo).

facts.fact: The Transvaal Colony paid for the new station in 1910 with surplus funds, just before the Union of South Africa was formed.
facts.quote: In 1910, shortly before the creation of the Union of South Africa, the government of the Transvaal Colony decided to spend excess funds on constructing a new station for Pretoria, rather than surrendering the money to the new national government.

facts.fact: It was Herbert Baker's first public building.
facts.quote: The new station was the first public building designed by Sir Herbert Baker.

facts.fact: A fire in 2001 destroyed almost all of the roof, but the structure survived.
facts.quote: Almost all of the roof was destroyed, although the structure itself was saved.

facts.fact: The restoration, costing 18 million rand, ran from June 2001 to February 2002.
facts.quote: The restoration, which cost 18 million rand, started in June 2001 and finished in February 2002.

facts.fact: The Japan Ukiyo-e Museum is a private art museum in Matsumoto holding over 100,000 woodblock prints, regarded as the world's largest such collection.
facts.quote: The Japan Ukiyo-e Museum (日本浮世絵博物館, Nihon Ukiyo-e Hakubutsukan)(JUM) is a privately owned Japanese art museum in Matsumoto, Nagano Prefecture. It holds over 100,000 Japanese woodblock prints, regarded as the world's largest collection of this form of art.

facts.fact: It was founded in 1982 by Tokichi Sakai, from the family collection of ukiyo-e.
facts.quote: The Japan Ukiyo-e Museum was established in 1982 by Tokichi Sakai, a member of the Sakai merchant family, who have practiced business in Matsumoto for generations. It is based on collections of ukiyo-e owned by the family.

facts.fact: Its main building was designed by Kazuo Shinohara and extended in 1995 by Haba Kuniharu.
facts.quote: The museum's main building was designed by the architect Shinohara Kazuo (1925–2006) and extended in 1995 by the architect Haba Kuniharu.

facts.fact: It stands next to the Matsumoto Open Air Architectural Museum.
facts.quote: It is located next to the Matsumoto Open Air Architectural Museum.

facts.fact: Shinohara's work is known for lucidity and ephemerality and is seen as a strong influence on Toyo Ito.
facts.quote: His work is generally classified as having strong qualities of lucidity and ephemerality, and for these reasons is often seen as ideologically influential on Toyo Ito's work.

facts.fact: Iwasaki Art Museum opened in Ibusuki, Kagoshima Prefecture, in 1983.
facts.quote: Iwasaki Art Museum (岩崎美術館, Iwasaki bijutsukan) opened in Ibusuki, Kagoshima Prefecture, Japan, in 1983.

facts.fact: Designed by Fumihiko Maki, it sits in the gardens of a resort hotel; its collection includes Kuroda Seiki, Fujishima Takeji and Western painters.
facts.quote: Located in the gardens of a resort hotel and designed by Fumihiko Maki, the museum's collection includes works by Kuroda Seiki and Fujishima Takeji, as well as Western painters.

facts.fact: The adjacent Iwasaki Yoshie Craft Gallery opened in 1998.
facts.quote: The adjacent Iwasaki Yoshie Craft Gallery (岩崎芳江工芸館) was established by the bequest of Iwasaki Yoshie, wife of the museum's founder businessman Iwasaki Yohachirō (岩崎與八郎), and opened in 1998.

facts.fact: Photographs of the museum were used as the cover art of the album Kankyō Ongaku.
facts.quote: Pictures of Iwasaki Art Museum were used as the album art for the ambient music collection Kankyō Ongaku: Japanese Ambient, Environmental & New Age Music 1980-1990

facts.fact: Those photographs are by Osamu Murai.
facts.quote: The box set features images in the outer slipcase and inner sleeves by photographer Osamu Murai of the Iwasaki Art Museum, designed by architect Fumihiko Maki.

facts.fact: The Miyagi Museum of Art opened in Sendai in 1981.
facts.quote: The Miyagi Museum of Art (宮城県美術館, Miyagi-ken bijutsukan) opened in Sendai, Japan, in 1981.

facts.fact: Its collection focuses on art linked to Miyagi Prefecture and the Tōhoku region from the Meiji period on, and includes paintings by Kandinsky and Klee.
facts.quote: The collection has as its primary focus works associated with Miyagi Prefecture and the Tōhoku region more generally, from the Meiji period to the present day, and also includes paintings by Wassily Kandinsky and Paul Klee.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Kunio Maekawa.
facts.quote: The building was designed by Kunio Maekawa.

facts.fact: Unlike Tange and the Metabolists, Maekawa held back from megastructures and biomorphic forms.
facts.quote: In contrast to his younger colleagues such as Kenzō Tange and those associated with the Metabolism movement, Maekawa displayed a reticence towards the megastructures and biomorphic forms that approached the rapid growth of technological modernity with exuberance, and expressed concerns over the capacity of machines to undermine human skill and artistry in architectural labor.

facts.fact: The National Showa Memorial Museum is a national museum in Chiyoda, Tokyo, run by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare.
facts.quote: The National Showa Memorial Museum (昭和館, Shōwakan) is a national museum in Chiyoda, Tokyo, Japan, managed by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare.

facts.fact: It opened on 27 March 1999.
facts.quote: Originally to be named The War Victims Peace Commemoration Prayer Hall, the museum opened on 27 March 1999, partly in response to strong lobbying by the Japan War-Bereaved Families Association, whose headquarters are in the adjacent Kudan Hall.

facts.fact: The building was designed by Kiyonori Kikutake.
facts.quote: The museum building was designed by Japanese architect Kiyonori Kikutake.

facts.fact: It stands next to Kudanshita Station and the north entrance of Kitanomaru Park.
facts.quote: The Museum is located next to Kudanshita Station and the northern entrance to Kitanomaru Park.

facts.fact: Kikutake was one of the founders of the Japanese Metabolist group.
facts.quote: Kiyonori Kikutake (菊竹 清訓, Kikutake Kiyonori) (April 1, 1928 – December 26, 2011) was a prominent Japanese architect known as one of the founders of the Japanese Metabolist group.

facts.fact: The Memorial Cathedral for World Peace in Hiroshima is the principal church of the Catholic Diocese of Hiroshima, designed by Togo Murano.
facts.quote: The church was designed by Togo Murano. It  follows the Roman or Latin rite and serves as the principal church of the Diocese of Hiroshima (Dioecesis Hiroshimaensis カトリック広島教区) which was created in 1959 with the bull Qui arcano of Pope John XXIII.

facts.fact: Built in tribute to the victims of war and the atomic bomb, it was begun in 1950 and opened in 1954.
facts.quote: It was built in tribute to the victims of war and the atomic bomb that was dropped on the city. Father Enomiya-Lassalle, who was exposed to the atomic bomb in Hiroshima, began construction in 1950 and it opened in 1954.

facts.fact: The 1947 competition drew 177 designs but no winner; Murano, one of the jurors, ended up designing it.
facts.quote: A total of 177 designs were submitted from Japanese architects such as Kenzo Tange and Kunio Maekawa, but no overall winner was declared. Murano ended up doing the design although he was actually one of the jurors.

facts.fact: Its massing shows Auguste Perret's influence, while the dome over the sanctuary and the small round chapels echo Byzantine architecture.
facts.quote: The volumetric treatment of the design was influenced by Auguste Perret, whereas the inclusion of a circular dome over the sanctuary and small cylindrical chapels on either side of the main volume are echoes of Byzantine architecture.

facts.fact: The concrete post-and-beam frame with infill panels recalls traditional Japanese architecture.
facts.quote: The post-and-beam concrete frame with internal panels is reminiscent of traditional Japanese architecture as are the shapes of the windows penetrating the tower.

facts.fact: The infill bricks were made from earth containing ash from the atomic bomb, laid so their rough faces cast shadows.
facts.quote: The brick infills in this case were made from earth containing ashes from the atomic bomb and are laid so that their rough surfaces cast shadows across the façade.

facts.fact: It stands between Tange's Peace Memorial Park and Hiroshima Station.
facts.quote: The cathedral is situated between Tange's Peace Memorial Park and JR Hiroshima Station.

facts.fact: It has been an Important Cultural Property of Japan since 5 July 2006.
facts.quote: The Cathedral has been designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan since July 5, 2006.

facts.fact: Junzo Sakakura's selected works list Hashima City Hall, Gifu, in 1959.
facts.quote: 1959 Hashima City Hall, Gifu

facts.fact: Sakakura worked in Le Corbusier's atelier in Paris for seven years, rising to studio chief.
facts.quote: He rose to the position of studio chief during his seven-year stay in the studio.

facts.fact: Kunio Maekawa's works list the Okayama Prefectural Office of 1955.
facts.quote: 1955 Okayama Prefectural Office, Okayama, Okayama Prefecture

facts.fact: Shin Takamatsu's works list the Nima Sand Museum, 1990, in Oda, Shimane.
facts.quote: Nima Sand Museum, 1990, Oda, Shimane, Japan

facts.fact: Takamatsu was born in Nima, Shimane, in 1948.
facts.quote: Shin Takamatsu (born August 5, 1948 in Nima, Shimane) is a Japanese architect.

facts.fact: Hiroshi Hara's works list the Iida City Museum, 1988, in Iida, Nagano Prefecture.
facts.quote: 1988: Iida City Museum, Iida, Nagano Prefecture

facts.fact: Hiroshi Hara's works list the Miyagi Prefectural Library, 1998, in Sendai.
facts.quote: 1998: Miyagi Prefectural Library, Sendai, Miyagi Prefecture

facts.fact: Okayama Symphony Hall is a concert hall in Okayama that opened in 1991 and seats 2,001.
facts.quote: Okayama Symphony Hall (岡山シンフォニーホール, Okayama Shinfonī Hōlu) is a concert hall in Okayama, Okayama, Japan. It opened in 1991 and seats 2,001.

facts.fact: Yoshinobu Ashihara was the architect, with acoustic design by Nagata Acoustics.
facts.quote: Yoshinobu Ashihara was the architect, with acoustical design by Nagata Acoustics.

facts.fact: Ashihara studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard and worked for Marcel Breuer.
facts.quote: After graduating from Harvard in 1953 with a master's degree in Architecture, Ashihara worked in the architectural practice of modernist Marcel Breuer.
